headline: Deloitte Announces Sustainability Fusion to Quantify, Communicate Sustainable Business Value - Press release | Deloitte US
summary_text: Deloitte Announces Sustainability Fusion to Quantify, Communicate Sustainable Business Value - Press release | Deloitte US ... # Deloitte Announces Framework, Digital Asset to Quantify, Communicate Sustainable Business Value ## Built in collaboration with Aspen Institute, “Sustainability Fusion” bridges sustainability and finance, enabling faster, more confident investment decisions for clients NEW YORK, July 14, 2026 — Deloitte today unveiled Sustainability Fusion TM, a new framework, digital tool, service offering and web-based evaluator designed to help the C-suite, particularly chief sustainability officers (CSOs) and chief financial officers (CFOs), unlock enterprise value by measuring and communicating how sustainability investments drive business outcomes. As sustainability becomes increasingly embedded in core business strategy, organizations should translate initiatives into the financial metrics and language required for capital allocation decisions. While sustainability investments are often assessed through compliance and reporting frameworks, those approaches are designed for different objectives than evaluating business value and investment performance. Sustainability Fusion introduces a method for positioning sustainability investments within the same value-creation logic used for any other business investment. Developed by Deloitte through convenings hosted by the Aspen Institute’s Business & Society Program and its network of sustainability and finance leaders, the framework is informed by a working group of more than 25 leaders from corporations, NGOs and independent advisers. To bring Sustainability Fusion to life, Deloitte also launched an AI-enabled, web-based evaluator that allows organizations to apply the framework to any sustainability investment and identify where enterprise value can be created across the business. ... - Evaluate sustainability investments using standard financial principles, including cost, revenue and risk, to better assess potential returns. - Translate sustainability assumptions into cash-flow impacts to improve decision clarity and credibility, harnessing tax-adjusted cash flow (TACF) as the core metric for expressing incremental value. - Create a repeatable, enterprise-wide approach for prioritizing and comparing investments. - Bridge cross-functional alignment between sustainability, finance and executive leadership. “Organizations need this framework now more than ever as sustainability and finance leaders are increasingly expected to quantify sustainability investments,” said Bill Marquard, Sustainability Fusion co-lead, Deloitte Consulting LLP. “When sustainability and finance are equipped to speak the same language, they’re able to unlock cost savings, reduce risk and generate new commercial pipelines seamlessly.” ... “Sustainability leaders don’t need a new set of metrics; they need a better way to connect their work to what drives business performance,” said Laura Bryce, Sustainability Fusion co-lead, Deloitte Consulting LLP. “When organizations can clearly articulate the financial value of sustainability investments, they can make decisions with greater confidence, move more quickly on priorities, and build competitive advantage in an increasingly dynamic business environment.” Sustainability Fusion is designed to complement existing reporting frameworks by translating sustainability efforts into the financial logic that underpins enterprise value. In doing so, it empowers CSOs and CFOs to jointly evaluate trade-offs, prioritize investments, and unlock the full business potential of sustainability.

headline: Bloomberg Launches Comprehensive CLO Reference Data Solution, Connecting Insights Across the Investment Lifecycle
summary_text: # Bloomberg Launches Comprehensive CLO Reference Data Solution, Connecting Insights Across the Investment Lifecycle ... Bloomberg Launches Comprehensive ... Reference Data Solution, Connecting Insights Across the Investment Lifecycle ... Integrated enterprise offering brings together normalized CLO and loan-level reference data with regulatory, liquidity and credit risk datasets, aligned with desktop workflows on the Bloomberg Terminal NEW YORK, Sept. 23, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Bloomberg today announced the launch of its Collateralized Loan Obligations (CLO) Data solution, delivering comprehensive, high-quality and normalized reference datasets for CLO market participants. Available for use across the enterprise through Bloomberg Data License, the solution includes loan-level data that gives clients access to insights on every loan held within a CLO portfolio, and can be seamlessly combined with Bloomberg's regulatory, risk, and sustainability data, and pricing and analytics for deeper analysis. The new solution aligns with CLO data available on the Bloomberg Terminal via functions such as LLD and CPR, supporting consistent workflows across enterprise and desktop environments. It is also accessible via Bloomberg Query Language (BQL), and Bloomberg plans to make this structured reference and loan-level data available in ASKB, the Bloomberg Terminal's new conversational AI interface, enabling customers to screen CLO collateral, compare key collateral characteristics, and conduct cross-deal analysis. Over time, ASKB is also expected to incorporate insights from offering documents, allowing users to evaluate key deal terms alongside the underlying collateral. Bloomberg's CLO Data solution provides CLO coverage with detailed structure and underlying loan-level collateral data across global markets. Customers can access security master data as well as other key information such as identifiers, payment information and deal structures, and advanced data points including coverage tests and tranche level performance indicators. The data supports workflows including deal and tranche discovery, cross-deal analysis, cash-flow modeling, risk assessment, performance analysis, security master maintenance and lifecycle tracking. While the CLO market has grown significantly in size, complexity and global reach, the supporting data infrastructure has not consistently kept pace. Information remains fragmented across offering ... , trustee reports, dealer runs and other proprietary systems, making it challenging for market participants to maintain a consistent, timely view of ... Bloomberg's CLO Loan Level Data package is interoperable with Bloomberg CLO Reference Data, Syndicated Loan Reference Data and Entity Reference Data. By normalizing reported holdings and mapping Financial Instrument Global Identifiers (FIGIs), Bloomberg enables customers to move efficiently from the CLO tranche and deal level to the underlying loan exposure and associated corporate entity, making the data easier to link, analyze and scale across workflows. Bloomberg's CLO Data solution integrates with Bloomberg's broader Enterprise Data offerings in a unified data model, allowing clients to combine CLO and loan level information with complementary liquidity, regulatory and credit risk data. The solution is supported by Bloomberg's global team of analysts, who source information directly from involved market participants and company filings such as prospectus and trustee reports. Bloomberg's quality control framework is designed to support the accuracy, integrity and timeliness of these datasets, with key metrics validated for consistency across cash flows and descriptive data and outlier detection algorithms used to help identify potential anomalies. Bloomberg Data License customers can browse and access this content at data.Bloomberg.com, and Bloomberg Terminal customers can enter DATA on the Bloomberg Terminal and have it delivered via SFTP, REST API or into a cloud environment of their choice. The same comprehensive CLO reference data is also available via Bloomberg's real-time market data feed, B-PIPE, and Bloomberg Enterprise Products. By bringing together data and workflows across the Terminal and Enterprise, Bloomberg is building a comprehensive front-to-back solution for the CLO market. The result is greater transparency across CLO structures and the underlying loan portfolios that support them.

headline: Bloomberg Launches Comprehensive CLO Reference Data Solution, Connecting Insights Across the Investment Lifecycle
summary_text: NEW YORK, Sept. 23, 2026 /PRNewswire/ - Bloomberg today announced the launch of its Collateralized Loan Obligations (CLO) Data solution, delivering comprehensive, high-quality and normalized reference datasets for CLO market participants. Available for use across the enterprise through Bloomberg Data License, the solution includes loan-level data that gives clients access to insights on every loan held within a CLO portfolio, and can be seamlessly combined with Bloomberg's regulatory, risk, and sustainability data, and pricing and analytics for deeper analysis. The new solution aligns with CLO data available on the Bloomberg Terminal via functions such as LLD < GO > and CPR < GO >, supporting consistent workflows across enterprise and desktop environments. It is also accessible via Bloomberg Query Language (BQL) , and Bloomberg plans to make this structured reference and loan-level data available in ASKB, the Bloomberg Terminal's new conversational AI interface, enabling customers to screen CLO collateral, compare key collateral characteristics, and conduct cross-deal analysis. Over time, ASKB is also expected to incorporate insights from offering documents, allowing users to evaluate key deal terms alongside the underlying collateral.

headline: NFU Mutual Selects Bloomberg and Clearwater Analytics for Front-to-Back Investment Management Workflow
summary_text: LONDON and NEW YORK, Sept. 22, 2026 /PRNewswire/ - Bloomberg and Clearwater Analytics ('Clearwater' ) today announced that NFU Mutual ('NFUM' ), the UK's leading rural insurer, has selected Bloomberg Buy-side Solutions together with the Clearwater platform to modernize its investment operating model. Managing approximately $ 32 billion in assets across a diversified range of funds, NFUM will jointly implement Bloomberg Buy-Side Solutions and Clearwater to streamline its front-to-back multi-asset investment management operating model. Bloomberg will provide portfolio management, trading, pre-trade compliance and trade operations - including workflows to support T+1 settlement readiness - while Clearwater will provide investment operations and investment accounting, with Bloomberg and Clearwater jointly supporting the client's regulatory reporting requirements. Bloomberg's strategic collaboration with Clearwater enables NFUM to establish a seamless, flexible front-to-back composable operating model that improves workflow efficiency, strengthens data consistency, and transaction reporting, and accelerates settlement cycles. " By adopting Bloomberg and Clearwater's integrated solutions, we are building an automated and highly flexible end-to-end operating model that strengthens our control environment, streamlines processes and builds a solid data foundation for our investment reporting ," said Nigel Bryan, Head of Financial Control at NFU Mutual.

headline: Bloomberg Electronic Markets Bring Full Programmatic Execution Support to FX Options Trading
summary_text: LONDON, Sept. 14, 2026 /PRNewswire/ - Bloomberg today launched its FX Options RFQ API on FXGO, its award-winning electronic foreign exchange trading solution. FXGO is part of Bloomberg Electronic Markets, and the introduction of this new offering brings end-to-end programmatic RFQ trading to the buy-side FX options market for the first time. Building on the popularity of FXGO's recently released Python-API FX Options ticket launcher, buy-side traders can now run the entire RFQ workflow programmatically, from submitting a trade request and receiving competing dealer quotes, to completing the deal, with no manual steps required at any stage. The launch covers vanilla and exotic FX options strategies across deliverable and non-deliverable currency markets and connects clients to FXGO's multi-dealer pool of liquidity providers through a single API. Bloomberg introduced its FX Options RFQ API to meet increased demand from systematic hedge funds and asset managers seeking to extend programmatic execution support into derivatives; Bloomberg recorded more than 58 % year-on-year growth since August 2025 in FX options volumes on FXGO, with hedge fund activity up more than 75 %.

The launch comes as Bloomberg marks 30 years in India and strengthens its digital presence in the country, which has now become the second-largest audience market globally for Bloomberg.com. In retrospect, while the war increased commodity pricing and spreads, Young said, for several petrochemicals and polymers, “there was probably an overreaction in March [and] April on [polymer] purchases, expanding margins and volumes significantly.” And while margins and volumes are yet to rebound, “we’re beginning to see some signs,” even as some Asian countries remain cautious after “learning from the lessons in April of accumulating excessive inventories,” Young said ... Whenever inventories do begin to normalize, renewed buying “could definitely support margins” if the war-related disruptions continue. ... Despite the uncertain future of Mexico’s longtime status as a valued US trade ally, Young expressed support for the outcome of two US Trade Representative (USTR) investigations. Young noted that although at the time of the call, the US had not yet announced a decision on Section 301 tariffs, Alpek expected a continuation of the underlying tariff of 10% on Mexican imports into the US. Later the same day, the USTR announced that 60 economies including Mexico, Canada and the EU, would be subject to a 10% tariff as of July 24. The current administration alleges that the affected countries and regions have failed to effectively prohibit the use of forced labor practices. Alpek also is awaiting the outcome of a second USTR investigation, looking at structural overcapacity and production in manufacturing sectors. Young said that although ultimately the investigations aim to provide fair trade conditions for producers in the US, there still is strong domestic competition in the market. And although he said it’s too early to forecast the impact of the latest round of tariffs, the company expects the tariffs will “address some of the distortions in the markets and bring a fair level of pricing for producers of PET and many other industries.” Additionally, with the US deciding against renewing the current terms of the US-Mexico-Canada Agreement (USMCA) this month, the trade pact now shifts into an annual review process. However, Alpek does not expect significant headwinds, because most chemicals made in Mexico use US feedstocks “that are fully compliant with the USMCA requirements and will be fully compliant with the rules of origin. So we expect continuity from USMCA.”

Woolworths Group Limited (ASX: WOW) private-label products, along with the Italian family-owned Mutti brand, passed the same country-of-origin test. The unresolved question is not whether a single tomato paste line survives the news cycle, but whether the Coles Group private-label sourcing model can absorb a Modern Slavery Act 2018 overlay, a regulator-level country-of-origin follow-up and a rival that has just been handed a traceability marketing gift, without compressing the margin advantage that makes private label the fastest-growing part of the shelf. ... Private-label penetration is not a peripheral part of the Coles Group model. It is a structural margin lever. Home-brand products carry higher gross margins than branded equivalents, and their expansion has been central to how Coles Group has defended earnings during the current cost-of-living cycle. A traceability event that questions the credibility of the Coles-brand label sits directly on the part of the business that has been earning the incremental margin. It also sits inside a Country of Origin Food Labelling Information Standard 2016 regime that gives the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission and state fair-trading agencies enforcement scope well beyond a reputational hit. ... The Modern Slavery Act 2018 requires large Australian retailers to publish annual statements identifying modern slavery risks in their supply chains and describing the actions taken to mitigate those risks. Coles Group, Woolworths Group and Aldi Australia all file Modern Slavery Act statements, and the Attorney-General’s Department maintains a public register of those statements. A Source Certain result that alleges Xinjiang-origin material moved through the private-label tomato paste supply chain would, if sustained, sit uncomfortably inside those statements. ... Coles Group and Aldi Australia. In a market where the two listed grocers are locked in continuous private-label share competition, that is a marketing asset Woolworths Group can convert quickly. Chief executive officer Amanda Bardwell has anchored the H1 FY26 message on value and execution, and a defensible traceability story on ... The near-term risk for Coles Group is not a customer exodus. It is a slower run rate of new private-label launches while procurement, quality assurance and legal teams reprocess the tomato paste supplier base and reassess the isotope-testing evidence chain. Every week the story sits open, Woolworths Group has more room to lead on the private-label conversation, and Aldi Australia has less room to expand share on price alone. Independent grocer Metcash Limited (ASX: MTS), which supplies IGA and Foodland, was not named in the Australian Broadcasting Corporation report and could see peripheral share benefits in categories where consumers actively reject Xinjiang-linked supply chains. ... The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission’s Federal Court action against Coles Group and Woolworths Group over allegedly misleading “prices dropped” and “down, down” promotions has dominated the regulatory framing of the supermarket sector since September 2024, and both companies have defended those proceedings. The Australian Broadcasting Corporation tomato paste findings are a different vector. Where the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission action alleges misconduct on the pricing side of the shelf, the Australian Broadcasting Corporation investigation alleges misconduct on the origin-declaration side of the shelf. The two vectors are unrelated in law but reinforcing in narrative, because the underlying question for the consumer is the same: can the label on the product be trusted. For investors, this means the discount that Coles Group is currently trading with relative to a clean traceability, clean pricing baseline may already be visible in the multiple. Coles Group closed intraday July 27, 2026 at A$23.45, up 0.09%, with a market capitalisation of A$31.60 billion, a price-earnings multiple of 31.08, an EPS of A$0.76, a 52-week range of A$20.10 to A$24.59 and a fully franked dividend yield of 3.11%. The stock is closer to the top of its range than the bottom. That leaves limited cushion for a further overhang, and the July 17, 2026 withdrawal from the Greencross Pet Wellness Company acquisition process, framed by the company as capital discipline, has removed one of the near-term growth optionalities that could have offset a private-label reputational drag. ... Coles Group has recovered from an A$20.10 52-week low to trade within 5% of its A$24.59 52-week high. It carries a price-earnings multiple that is above its long-run average, supported by consistent dividend growth and an H1 FY25 print that delivered A$23.04 billion in sales (up 3.7%) and A$666 million in underlying net profit after tax (up 6.4%). Broker consensus has moved higher through the year, with Bell Potter’s most recent public price target at A$20.50 (a lag versus current market), Ord Minnett at A$19.50 (also lag versus current market) and multiple houses upgrading through the June and July windows on the value-perception recovery in Australian food retail. Business News Today did not identify a widely published current broker consensus that has yet formally incorporated the Australian Broadcasting Corporation supply-chain findings. That gap between the recovery in the share price and the emerging supply-chain narrative is where the near-term risk lives. If the story broadens into a regulator response or a formal retailer product-withdrawal cycle, the recovery in the multiple is exposed to a re-rating that broker models have not yet reflected. If Coles Group can produce credible internal forensic testing that rebuts the Source Certain findings within the next reporting window, the current multiple can hold. The intermediate scenario, in which the story fades without formal resolution, is the most likely, and the least useful for the investor thesis. ... The first signal is whether Coles Group publishes an independent verification report on the flagged private-label lines within the next quarterly result window. The second signal is whether the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission or the Department of Agriculture, Fisheries and Forestry open an inquiry into country-of-origin labelling for imported processed tomato products. The third signal is whether Woolworths Group actively markets its clean result, which would compress Coles Group’s private-label share momentum. The fourth signal is whether Simplot Australia and other Coles Group private-label processors adjust their tomato paste sourcing, and whether that adjustment shows up in category shelf pricing over the next two to three quarters. The fifth signal is whether the Modern Slavery Act 2018 statements for 2026 filed by Coles Group and Woolworths Group carry materially different levels of forensic-testing disclosure.

headline: In 2021, Australia's RMIT helped Coles put 900,000 pieces of soft plastic into concrete. 1 year later, another Coles development was set to reuse 6.5 million pieces through Polyrok
summary_text: In 2021, Australia's RMIT helped Coles put 900,000 pieces of soft plastic into concrete. 1 year later, another Coles development was set to reuse 6.5 million pieces through Polyrok. Soft plastic such as wrappers, cling wrap and plastic bags has been difficult to recycle. RMIT University worked with Coles and Victorian recycling organisations to develop Polyrok, a plastic aggregate made from recycled soft plastics for use in concrete.The material was first used commercially at a Coles car park in Horsham. A larger application was announced in February 2021 for a Coles supermarket development at Cobblebank in Melbourne, where more than 6.5 million pieces of soft plastic were set to be recycled through Polyrok.How Polyrok was developedRMIT engineers worked with Replas, RED Group and SR Engineering to develop the mix methodology and characterise the Polyrok material.The project was led by RMIT Senior Lecturer Dr Jonathan Tran and his team from the School of Engineering.One of the challenges was getting plastic and concrete to bond effectively. He said, "Glass can be easily recycled and turned into things such as sand replacement, but plastic is much harder ," adding, "Mixing concrete and plastic is difficult, as the two do n't naturally bond, as quoted by RMIT.Researchers used X-ray computed tomography to help design the concrete mix, with the aim of optimising its strength and acoustic energy absorption.RMIT described Polyrok as a sustainable aggregate alternative with enhanced durability that was lighter to work with.133978447The Horsham car parkThe Coles Horsham car park was the first commercial construction project in Australia to use Polyrok.The material was made from plastic bags and soft plastic packaging recovered through the REDcycle program and used as an alternative to aggregate minerals in concrete.RMIT reported that more than 900,000 pieces of plastic packaging were saved from landfill and incorporated into the car park concrete.The Cobblebank developmentOn February 15, 2021, Coles announced that more than 6.5 million pieces of soft plastic would be recycled through Polyrok as part of its supermarket development at Cobblebank in Melbourne's west.Coles described the project as the largest-ever commercial application of Polyrok at the time.The soft plastic came from plastic bags and packaging recovered through the REDcycle program.133973739A larger opportunity for soft plastic recyclingSince the partnership began, Tran said Replas, RED Group and Coles had diverted more than 1.3 billion pieces of soft plastic from landfill.He also said there was potential for 105,000 tonnes of soft plastics to be converted into dense plastic aggregate each year at a local factory in Melbourne, as quoted by RMIT.The RMIT research team included Tran and research fellows Dr Rajeev Roychand and Dr Thomas Loh.Tran said the team hoped to explore producing sustainable concrete structures using a new large-scale concrete 3D printer at RMIT's Bundoora campus.

headline: EU Aluminium Scrap Duty Axed — Recycling Bets at Risk

By Branka Narancic - 23 September 2026 ... - Constellium's 130 million euro, 130,000-tonne Neuf-Brisach recycling centre is already operational, but the company's next wave of recycling investments across packaging, automotive, and aerospace segments remains uncommitted, with scrap feedstock availability cited as the binding input to those decisions. - Three variables will determine whether the framework holds: how many of the 32 non-OECD exemption applicants are approved in the November 2026 finalisation, whether OECD-destination flows such as Turkey are addressed, and whether Constellium confirms or suspends its evaluation-stage projects within a 12-month horizon. ... Over 1.25 million tonnes of aluminium scrap left Europe in 2024, a 51% rise since 2019, and the window to redirect that feedstock into domestic recycling infrastructure is closing as the November 2026 finalisation of the revised Waste Shipment Regulation approaches. Constellium’s Neuf-Brisach recycling centre, a €130 million facility opened in September 2024, shows exactly what domestic capacity looks like, and exactly what stalls if scrap cannot be secured. ... The revised Waste Shipment Regulation, Regulation (EU) 2024/1157, establishes the legal framework governing cross-border waste movements including the non-OECD export ban and the country-level exemptions process that will determine scrap availability inside Europe from May 2027. Here is the mechanism that replaces the duty. From 21 May 2027, the WSR will ban exports of non-hazardous waste, including aluminium scrap, to non-OECD countries. Destinations can escape the ban if they demonstrate they manage the material to standards equivalent to EU environmental rules, granted through a case-by-case exemptions process. That structural difference matters more than it first appears. A duty changes export economics directly for every shipment, everywhere. The company said it has largely locked in scrap needs for the third quarter and much of the fourth quarter at favorable levels. ... Joerg said aerospace demand has run ahead of Constellium’s initial expectations for the year, supported by record commercial aircraft backlogs, rising aircraft deliveries and efforts by original equipment manufacturers to increase build rates. headline: Constellium sees revenue, net income increase Q2 - Recycling Today
summary_text: Paris-based Constellium has posted strong second-quarter and half-year results that include record profitability, significantly increased earnings and solid cash flow, causing the aluminum products and recycling company to raise its full-year outlook. In the second quarter, Constellium reported $2.7 billion in revenue, a 31 percent increase from the second quarter of 2025, while its net income was $148 million compared with net income of $36 million a year earlier. Adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization (EBITDA) totaled $439 million, which the company credits to stronger results in each of its operating segments—Aerospace & Transportation (A&T), Packaging & Automotive Rolled Products (P&ARP) and Automotive Structures & Industry (AS&I)— a favorable change in the noncash metal price lag impact and favorable foreign exchange translation, partially offset by higher corporate costs. At 381,000 metric tons, however, Constellium’s shipments for the quarter were 1 percent lower than in the second quarter of 2025. For the first half of this year, Constellium reported shipments of 751,000 metric tons, down 1 percent from the first half of last year, while revenue was $5.2 billion (a 28 percent increase year over year) and net income was $344 million compared with $74 million the first half of 2025. The company reported adjusted EBITDA of $798 million, an increase of $466 million compared with the first half of 2025. “Constellium delivered a new record quarterly adjusted EBITDA in the second quarter despite uncertainties on the macroeconomic and geopolitical fronts,” says CEO Ingrid Joerg. “We achieved stronger financial performance across all of our operating segments again this quarter, including record quarterly segment adjusted EBITDA at our A&T and P&ARP segments.” She adds that the company benefited from improved market dynamics, including improvements in the aerospace and transportation, industry and defense (TID) environment, automotive rolled products supply shortages in North America and healthy recycling performance in North America and Europe. "Even though the current landscape remains volatile, we have a strong track record of navigating and executing in any environment,” Joerg says. “Based on our current outlook, we are raising our guidance for 2026 and now expect adjusted EBITDA in the range of $980 million–$1.02 billion, excluding the noncash impact of metal price lag, and free cash flow in excess of $300 million.” She adds that Constellium expects to achieve its 2028 targets of $900 million in adjusted EBITDA and free cash flow of $300 million, two years ahead of schedule. ... The A&T segment saw a 21 percent year-over-year increase in shipments during the quarter, reaching 65,000 metric tons. Segment adjusted EBITDA totaled $135 million, an increase of 61 percent year over year. For the first half, the A&T segment realized adjusted EBITDA of $238 million, an increase of 44 percent compared with the first half of 2025, shipments totaled 125,000 metric tons, a 20 percent increase from the first half of last year. Constellium’s P&ARP segment saw adjusted EBITDA increase by 123 percent year over year in the second quarter to $165 million; however, shipments of 266,000 metric tons reflected a decrease of 4 percent mainly due to lower shipments of packaging rolled products, partially offset by higher shipments of automotive rolled products, which benefited from supply shortages in North America. Revenue was $1.7 billion, an increase of 36 percent compared to the second quarter of 2025. For the first half of 2026, P&ARP adjusted EBITDA was $317 million, an increase of 135 percent compared with the first half of 2025, while shipments of 527,000 metric tons reflected a decrease of 3 percent compared to the first half of 2025. Revenue was $3.2 billion, an increase of 30 percent year over year. AS&I segment adjusted EBITDA was $26 million, an increase of 44 percent compared with the second quarter of 2025, while shipments of 55,000 metric tons were flat due to stable shipments of automotive and other extruded products. Revenue was $458 million, an increase of 9 percent compared with the second quarter of 2025. Segment adjusted EBITDA was $49 million for the first half of this year, an increase of 44 percent compared with the first half of 2025, which Costellium attributes to lower operating costs and favorable foreign exchange translation, partially offset by lower shipments and unfavorable price and mix. Shipments of 105,000 metric tons reflected a decrease of 2 percent compared with the first half of 2025, mainly from lower shipments of automotive and other extruded products. Revenue was $873 million, an increase of 9 percent compared with a year earlier.

Constellium record earnings in the first quarter show how favourable North American aluminium market conditions are lifting margins even when shipment volumes remain flat. The France-based downstream aluminium producer reported segment-adjusted Ebitda of $359mn, up 93% from a year earlier. The company’s revenue rose by 24% to $2.5bn in January-March, while total shipments slipped by 1% to 370,000t. This split matters because Constellium’s performance was driven less by volume growth and more by pricing, product mix, recycling economics and supply shortages in key end markets. Constellium record earnings were strongest in packaging and automotive rolled products, where North American supply tightness created better commercial conditions. Aerospace and transport also improved, supported by stronger customer activity and rising shipments. ... Constellium’s packaging and automotive rolled products division delivered the largest earnings improvement. Ebitda rose by 152% on the year to $151mn, while revenue increased by 24% to $1.48bn. ... North America was the key driver. Constellium benefited from a supply shortage in automotive rolled products, which improved pricing power and margins for qualified suppliers. ... Constellium also benefited from better US recycling margins. Trade tariffs affected aluminium products but not scrap, improving the relative economics of recycled inputs. ... The first-quarter result therefore shows how recycling and trade policy can reinforce each other. Tariffs changed product economics, while scrap availability gave Constellium a stronger cost position. ... Constellium’s aerospace and transport division also performed strongly. Ebitda rose by 24% to $102mn, while revenue increased by 30% to $609mn. Shipments in the segment rose by 18% to 60,000t. This was the clearest volume-growth signal across the company’s business units. ... , wings, transport systems and lightweight design ... The automotive structures and industry division posted Ebitda of $24mn, up 50% from a year earlier. Revenue rose by 9% to $415mn, while shipments fell by 3% to 51,000t. This again shows the importance of mix and margin. Constellium improved earnings even where volumes declined, suggesting stronger commercial discipline and better end-market positioning. The company raised its 2026 adjusted Ebitda guidance to $900mn-940mn. Chief executive Ingrid Joerg said macroeconomic and geopolitical uncertainty remains, but the company is optimistic about its end-market positioning. Constellium record earnings therefore point to a market where quality of exposure matters more than headline volume. Packaging, automotive rolled products, aerospace and recycling-linked margins are driving performance. For the aluminium sector, the message is clear. Supply shortages, tariffs, scrap economics and aerospace recovery are reshaping profitability across downstream producers. > ### The Metalnomist Commentary > > Constellium’s quarter shows that aluminium value is moving toward qualified products, regional supply and recycling economics. The strongest performers will be producers that can combine technical approvals, scrap access and exposure to tight North American end markets.

headline: Constellium may halt EU recycling expansion over scrap shortage By Investing.com
summary_text: Investing.com -- Constellium said Tuesday it may cancel plans to expand aluminium recycling operations in the European Union if policymakers do not address a shortage of scrap metal caused by exports to overseas markets. CEO Ingrid Joerg told Reuters the company has multiple recycling projects under review across its packaging, automotive and aerospace divisions. The projects could be larger or smaller than a previous €130 million ($148.82 million) recycling expansion at its Neuf-Brisach plant in France. "We have several recycling projects in the pipeline that we are investigating. But if there’s no scrap, they’re not going to happen," Joerg said. The European Commission dropped plans this month to impose an export duty on aluminium scrap, which the industry says is needed to keep the low-cost raw material within Europe.

headline: Snowflake and STACKIT announce integration for data sovereignty in Europe · dutchstartup.ai
summary_text: Snowflake and STACKIT are partnering to offer sovereign data and AI services to businesses across Europe, with a focus on regulated sectors in Germany. STACKIT is the cloud platform of the Schwarz Group, the parent company of Lidl and Kaufland, and operates data centres exclusively in Germany and Austria. The collaboration fits into a broader movement in the European cloud market, where organisations in financial services, healthcare and the public sector are increasingly requiring that their data demonstrably stays within the EU and is not accessible to jurisdictions outside Europe. Both Snowflake and STACKIT have each been positioning themselves on this theme for some time, but a direct integration between the two platforms had not previously been announced. ... STACKIT was launched in 2018 as the internal cloud and colocation provider of the Schwarz Group and opened its doors to external customers in 2022. The platform currently operates three data centres: two in Germany, in Neckarsulm and Ellhofen, and one in Ostermiething, Austria. Additional availability zones near Heilbronn are under construction. With approximately 500 employees, STACKIT says it focuses on small and medium-sized enterprises and the public sector. The company uses OpenStack as the foundation for its cloud infrastructure and has previously announced partnerships with Google and SAP. In April 2026, STACKIT was selected by the European Commission as one of four cloud providers in a tender worth 180 million euros. ... Snowflake has been working for some time on expansion into what it describes as sovereign markets in Europe. The company announced it would place its first zonal archive outside the US within the EU, so that usage data from European customers is stored within the region. Snowflake is also developing stricter access controls through a regional support model. Snowflake is also a launch partner for the AWS European Sovereign Cloud, which is expected to go live in Brandenburg, Germany, by the end of 2025. The partnership with STACKIT aligns with that direction: by integrating with a European provider that keeps its infrastructure entirely within the EU, Snowflake can serve customers with stricter data residency requirements than a standard public cloud environment offers. Snowflake reports processing five billion queries per day and counted more than ten thousand customers in fiscal year 2024, including more than 700 companies from the Forbes Global 2000. That scale makes a sovereign variant for Europe relevant to a substantial segment of its customer base. ... The integration is explicitly aimed at sectors where compliance requirements carry significant weight, such as financial services, healthcare and government agencies. Germany has strict rules governing the processing of personal data and business-critical information, partly under the GDPR and sector-specific legislation such as the NIS2 Directive on network and information security. For organisations in these sectors, not only the location of the data matters, but also who can gain technical access to it. A cloud platform that is entirely European-owned and manages its infrastructure exclusively in Europe offers a legally distinct position compared with a European region of an American hyperscaler, where the right of access by US authorities under the CLOUD Act remains a recurring point of debate. STACKIT explicitly positions itself on this distinction. Whether the integration with Snowflake also provides technical isolation from Snowflake's US infrastructure and operations, and how that is legally guaranteed, cannot yet be assessed on the basis of the information available. ... The collaboration between Snowflake and STACKIT illustrates a pattern that recurs in the European cloud market: large international software companies seek ties with European infrastructure providers to serve customers who, for legal or political reasons, do not wish to rely on an entirely American cloud stack. Earlier examples include partnerships between American technology companies and providers such as OVHcloud, Deutsche Telekom and T-Systems. For Dutch and European founders, investors and policymakers, it is relevant that the market for sovereign cloud infrastructure is in flux. The European Commission is actively stimulating this segment, including through tenders in which European origin and data residency are weighted factors. STACKIT's selection by the Commission in April 2026 for a contract worth 180 million euros shows that European cloud providers are being found competitive against the major American vendors in public procurement. The question remains which technical and legal standards will ultimately become the norm for what 'sovereign' truly means in practice.

headline: Snowflake (SNOW) Is Growing Faster Now Than It Was A Year Ago - Insider Monkey
summary_text: On September 2, Snowflake (NYSE: SNOW) reported second-quarter fiscal 2027 results that showed an unusual pattern for a company of its size: growth speeding up rather than slowing down. Product revenue hit $1.49 billion, up 37% year over year, and it was the third straight quarter that growth rate climbed instead of fading. Total revenue reached $1.55 billion, a 35% increase from the same period last year. ... Snowflake’s pitch has always centered on being the place enterprises store and govern their data, but AI is now pulling new workloads onto that platform and pushing existing customers to use more of it. Net revenue retention came in at 126%, meaning customers already on Snowflake are spending well beyond what they paid a year earlier, driven by fresh migrations and new AI use cases. The company added 692 net new customers in the quarter, a 32% jump in the pace of additions compared to the same quarter last year, and its roster of high-value customers, those spending more than $1 million annually, grew 27% to 828. Two AI products are doing a lot of that work. CoCo, which brings governed AI and coding agents to data operations, is now used by more than 9,100 accounts after adding over 2,000 net new accounts in the quarter alone. CoWork, which lets people query enterprise data in plain language, has reached 5,800 accounts. Customer Sayari used CoCo to migrate 12 billion records to an AI-ready foundation and cut costs by more than 50%, while an Australian financial institution reported tenfold faster query performance after moving its financial crime platform onto Snowflake. Management raised full-year product revenue guidance to $6.07 billion, up from a prior estimate of $5.84 billion, and lifted its non-GAAP operating margin guidance to 14.5% from 13.5%, with margin already expanding to 15.3% in the quarter from 11% a year earlier. ... The growth is not free of trade-offs. CFO Brian Robins told investors the revised outlook “includes a higher revenue mix from fast-growing AI workloads which carry a lower contribution margin today,” a direct acknowledgment that the fastest-growing part of the business is also the least profitable part right now. Non-GAAP product gross margin came in at 74.7%, and the shift toward AI is the reason it is not higher. Robins also flagged that bookings are expected to be “increasingly weighted towards the fourth quarter,” a seasonal pattern that can make remaining performance obligations, which stood at $9 billion and grew 30% year over year, look lumpier from quarter to quarter than the underlying business really is. Roughly 54% of that $9 billion is expected to convert to revenue over the next 12 months, and while that recognition rate rose 42% from the prior year’s estimate, it also means nearly half the backlog sits further out, subject to renewal timing that management itself says is shifting later in the year. ... Hedge fund ownership climbed to 103 funds holding Snowflake, up from 80 the prior quarter, a notable pickup in institutional interest. Short interest sits at 5.25% of float, a level that suggests a real but not dominant bear camp rather than heavy organized skepticism. The stock’s forward P/E of 166.67, as of September 11, shows the market is pricing in a lot of future earnings growth rather than valuing the company on what it earns today. That combination points to a market that largely believes the acceleration story management just delivered, even as the number itself leaves little room for a stumble. ... Snowflake’s quarter answered the question that mattered most: whether AI adoption actually shows up in the numbers, and it did, across revenue growth, customer additions, and margin expansion all at once. The open question is whether that growth can keep compounding without dragging product gross margins down further as AI workloads make up a bigger share of the mix. For the growth story to keep working, CoCo and CoWork need to keep pulling in new accounts at their current pace.

headline: The Flywheel Is Back at Snowflake — CoWork and CoCo Are Why — The Signal
summary_text: Snowflake's AI Data Cloud now runs the agents doing enterprise work: CoWork answers questions with cited sources, CoCo writes production code, and both meter compute. Product revenue grew 37% in Q2 FY27 — a third straight quarter of acceleration — and shares jumped more than 20% at the open. By Chino Iruke Sep 3, 2026 4 min Two years ago, the knock on Snowflake was easy to summarize: the AI boom was happening everywhere except on its income statement. Then came a quarter that flipped the script — and another, and another. Product growth ran roughly 30% in Q4 FY26, hit 34% in Q1 FY27, and just landed at 37% for Q2. When Snowflake reported after the close on September 2, shares jumped more than 20% at the open and tagged a fresh 52-week high. The comeback has a name, and it's not a spreadsheet: it's agents. ... agentic era. The next wave of software isn't chatbots that ... questions — it' ... autonomous agents doing multi-step work ... . But no sane enterprise lets an agent roam freely over customer records, payroll, and proprietary models. Agents need guardrails and context, and Snowflake's ... is that it provides both: a governed layer where AI gets safe, permissioned access to the data that matters, every move audited, every query metered. Because Snowflake charges by consumption, more agent work means ... compute — and more compute means ... revenue. That's the flywheel, and this quarter it spun in public. ... Product revenue hit $1.49 billion in Q2 FY27, up 37% year over year — the third straight quarter of accelerating growth. Total revenue rose 35% to $1.55 billion, and non-GAAP EPS of $0.62 blew past the roughly $0.45 analysts expected, up 77%. Snowflake still reports a GAAP net loss — the beat lives on the non-GAAP lines the Street grades. Non-GAAP operating margin hit 15.3%, more than 400 basis points better than a year ago, and management says AI products drove roughly half of the acceleration. Then the guide went up again: full-year product revenue now $6.07 billion, up 36%, raised from the $5.84 billion guided last quarter, with Q3 pointed at $1.588 to $1.593 billion — growth of 37% to 38%. The stars are two products renamed at Snowflake's June Summit. CoWork — formerly Snowflake Intelligence — is the knowledge-worker agent: ask it anything about your enterprise data and it answers with cited sources, automates the multi-step follow-through, and can act inside Gmail, Jira, Slack, and Salesforce, all within Snowflake's governance. It's already in 5,800 accounts. CoCo — formerly Cortex Code — is Snowflake's coding agent, writing production code and pipelines natively. It just passed 9,100 accounts after adding 2,000 net new in Q2 alone. Management calls the pair the fastest-growing products Snowflake has ever shipped. The customer list backs up the hype. 1Password and Indeed signed on as AI-focused wins this quarter, and data intelligence firm Sayari says it cut costs by more than half while using CoCo to migrate 12 billion records. Total customers hit 14,554, up 692 net new and 32% year over year. And 828 customers now pay over $1 million a year on product, up 27%. Net revenue retention sits at 126% — a fifth straight quarter at or above 125% — and remaining performance obligations reached $9.00 billion, up 30%. CEO Sridhar Ramaswamy calls it compounding. "AI continues to compound our advantages, creating a flywheel effect," he says. "The Agentic Enterprise runs on Snowflake." The main rival, Databricks, stays private and formidable. Snowflake's counter is neutrality: agents and data that work across all three hyperscalers, governance baked in at the platform level, and a marketplace that moves data and models as easily as app stores move software. One nuance worth knowing: the AI-heavy mix trims product gross margin toward the roughly 74% guide even as operating margin expands. Growing faster, slightly less gross-profitable per AI dollar, more profitable overall — that's a trade worth taking. None of this is risk-free. Databricks is spending heavily on the same problem, agent economics are young, and the stock's valuation still assumes years of compounding. But three straight quarters of acceleration and guidance raised twice — Snowflake isn't chasing the agentic story anymore. It's writing it.

headline: CrowdStrike brings Falcon to Google Cloud & Snowflake
summary_text: CrowdStrike brings Falcon to Google ... # CrowdStrike brings Falcon to Google Cloud & Snowflake Tue, 1st Sep 2026 (Today) SEAN MITCHELL Publisher CrowdStrike has made its Falcon platform available on Google Cloud and through Snowflake Marketplace, extending the cybersecurity company's reach across cloud infrastructure and enterprise data services. Under the Google Cloud agreement, Falcon now runs on Google Cloud infrastructure, starting with regional infrastructure in the US. The setup is intended to give customers more choice over where they deploy the platform while addressing data sovereignty and localisation requirements. Under the Snowflake agreement, Falcon will be listed on Snowflake Marketplace. Snowflake customers will be able to apply pre-committed capacity to Falcon through the Marketplace Capacity Drawdown programme, linking cybersecurity spending to existing cloud data commitments. ... Falcon on Google Cloud is initially available in the US, with expansion to other Google Cloud regions planned later. In-region processing is aimed at customers that need data to remain within particular jurisdictions. ... Google Cloud framed the partnership around data sovereignty and AI workloads, both of which have become central concerns for regulated industries and multinational groups. As cloud usage expands, companies handling sensitive operational or customer information have sought more control over where data is processed. ... The Snowflake tie-up centres on procurement as well as data integration. By making Falcon available through Snowflake Marketplace, CrowdStrike is tapping a route that lets joint customers use existing Snowflake spending commitments rather than negotiate a separate purchasing path. That may appeal to finance and procurement teams looking to simplify software buying, especially as security budgets face greater scrutiny. For CrowdStrike, the arrangement opens another channel into enterprise accounts that already standardise on Snowflake for data storage, analysis and sharing. The companies also outlined several technical links between Falcon and Snowflake data. Federated search is intended to let analysts query Snowflake data directly from Falcon investigations, while Falcon Next-Gen SIEM will correlate Snowflake data with security telemetry. CrowdStrike also said Falcon Onum will route security telemetry to Snowflake as well as other destinations. ... Snowflake described the partnership as a way to bring broader enterprise context into security operations. "Enterprises already bring their most critical data to Snowflake, and that broader enterprise context is what makes security decisions better," said Mayank Upadhyay, Chief Security and Trust Officer, Snowflake. "Our collaboration with CrowdStrike will let security teams build stronger detections and run more complete investigations against data they already trust, without moving it." The two deals underline how cybersecurity suppliers are seeking tighter links with the platforms where enterprise data and computing workloads already sit. Rather than selling standalone tools alone, vendors are increasingly trying to place security controls inside major cloud and data ecosystems used across large organisations. For CrowdStrike, that means pursuing infrastructure alignment with Google Cloud as well as commercial and data integration with Snowflake. Together, the moves give the company another route into customers that want to keep security operations closer to their existing cloud estates and data environments. Image: Daniel Bernard

No-Headquarters/BOZEMAN, Mont. – Aug. 18, 2026 – Snowflake (NYSE: SNOW), the AI Data Cloud company, today announced dynamic model routing 2 within Cortex AI Gateway and Snowflake's flagship AI products, alongside expanded access to leading open models. Snowflake's innovations help enterprises reduce unnecessary AI spend and improve what Snowflake calls intelligence efficiency, measuring how effectively companies turn compute, models, data, and context into business impact. The new capabilities build on Cortex AI Gateway, which Snowflake announced in July 2026 as a unified foundation for governing agent connections, intelligently routing requests, and optimizing AI consumption. As companies deploy more AI apps and agents into production, using the same model for every task can drive up costs, while evaluating and managing a growing mix of models creates more work for development teams. Snowflake is addressing both challenges by making model selection more automatic and giving customers access to a broader range of open source and proprietary models. With the addition of dynamic model routing, Cortex AI Gateway can automatically select the specific model with the optimal balance of quality and cost for the task at hand. Dynamic model routing is also integrated across Snowflake's flagship AI products, including Snowflake CoCo and Snowflake CoWork, and is available to third-party AI agents using Cortex AI Gateway. This new capability directs lower-complexity or repetitive tasks to more efficient models, while work that requires deeper reasoning is routed to frontier models. This helps customers reduce unnecessary inference spend, without having to manage model selection for each request themselves. Snowflake will also be expanding customers' access to leading open models, including DeepSeek-V4-Flash 0731 1 and GLM-5.3 3, through Snowflake Cortex AI. This adds to Snowflake's extensive model library, giving customers even more options to balance model quality and cost, while keeping governed data secure within Snowflake. ... Cortex AI Gateway Delivers Better AI Economics Through Model Choice The addition of dynamic model routing in Cortex AI Gateway is designed to help enterprises use costly frontier models only when they materially improve an outcome across Snowflake CoCo, Snowflake CoWork, and third-party AI agents. Beyond automatically selecting a model for each request, dynamic model routing gives customers control over which models and providers are available to their users. This is particularly important for global organizations navigating regional model availability or for regulated industries with specific compliance requirements. As model performance and pricing change, Cortex AI Gateway can update routing decisions across Snowflake's AI products like Snowflake CoCo and Snowflake CoWork so customers don't need to rebuild their apps or agents. This allows enterprises to take advantage of new model options as they emerge while Snowflake manages the complexity of model choice and optimization underneath. ... Snowflake Introduces New Open Models to Governed Enterprise Data DeepSeek-V4-Flash 0731 and GLM-5.3 are the latest models that will be added to Snowflake's growing portfolio of models available across Cortex AI, Snowflake CoCo, and Snowflake CoWork. Together with models from providers including Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, SpaceXAI, Meta, and Mistral, this portfolio gives customers more freedom to choose the right combination of performance and cost for each workload. ... Snowflake's AI Research Team evaluated DeepSeek-V4-Flash on enterprise-focused tasks, with recent testing showing that DeepSeek v4 Flash outperformed the leading proprietary models used for the evaluation, scoring 74.4 percent on data engineering tasks. GLM-5.2 also performed strongly at 62.8 percent, while using fewer tokens than any other model tested 5. These results demonstrate that open models are increasingly capable of supporting mission-critical tasks at a lower cost. Snowflake Helps Enterprises Improve Intelligence Efficiency at Scale As enterprises use more models across a growing number of AI apps and agents, improving intelligence efficiency requires visibility and control over how AI resources are consumed. Cortex AI Gateway gives administrators visibility into token usage and costs, while allowing organizations to establish spending limits across AI apps and agents. Snowflake CoCo extends those controls through Snowflake's existing role-based access and tagging framework, allowing administrators to set default models, attribute usage to teams or cost centers, establish per-user quotas, and receive notifications as consumption approaches defined limits. Coupled with dynamic model routing and expanded model choice, these capabilities give enterprises greater control over their AI economics. Organizations can automatically match workloads to the right models, take advantage of new model options as they emerge, and manage how AI resources are consumed across the business. This helps enterprises improve intelligence efficiency while maintaining Snowflake's trusted governance and retaining ownership of their proprietary enterprise data and context. ... headline: Snowflake launches Cortex AI Gateway to control AI agents and prevent runaway enterprise costs | VentureBeat
summary_text: Snowflake launches Cortex AI Gateway to control AI agents and prevent runaway enterprise costs | VentureBeat # Snowflake launches Cortex AI Gateway to control AI agents and prevent runaway enterprise costs ... Snowflake announced Cortex AI Gateway on Tuesday, a centralized control layer designed to govern how AI agents — including those built by competitors like Anthropic's Claude Code and Cursor — access enterprise data, tools, and models. Alongside the gateway, the company unveiled a first wave of security integrations with 1Password, Aembit, Linx Security, SailPoint, and Saviynt, an unusual lineup of identity vendors who often compete with one another, now aligned around a shared trust model for autonomous agents. The announcement, made from the company's no-headquarters base in Bozeman, Montana, is Snowflake's most aggressive move yet to position itself not merely as the place where enterprise data lives, but as the control plane that decides what AI agents are allowed to do with it. ... Cortex AI Gateway, which will enter public preview soon, functions as a connective layer for what Snowflake calls "all trusted agent activity." It governs both first-party agents built inside Snowflake, such as Snowflake CoWork and CoCo, and third-party agents built on external platforms. With support for more than 100 MCP servers — the Model Context Protocol connectors that have become the de facto standard for wiring agents to enterprise tools — the gateway centralizes access policies, authentication, permissions, and audit logging in a single place. The gateway also addresses a less glamorous but increasingly urgent problem: runaway AI spending. It gives IT and finance teams a unified view of AI consumption, attributes costs to the specific teams, agents, or workloads driving them, and enforces spending limits before bills spiral. ... The gateway builds directly on Snowflake's May 2026 acquisition of Natoma, a 27-person startup whose centralized MCP gateway enforced identity, policy, and audit at the tool-call level. Forbes reported at the time that the deal — announced the same day as Snowflake's $1.33 billion quarterly product revenue report and a $6 billion AWS compute commitment — was the smallest of the day's three announcements by dollar value but the most revealing about where Snowflake believes the next platform fight sits: not in the data warehouse, but in the layer that decides what an agent may touch and records what it did. ... Perhaps the most striking aspect of today’s announcement is the roster. 1Password, SailPoint, Saviynt, Okta, and Aembit compete for overlapping identity and access budgets. Snowflake convinced them to build against a common trust framework anyway. ... There is self-interest in the openness, of course. Snowflake sits atop an enormous concentration of sensitive enterprise data — more than 13,900 customers, by the company's count — and every third-party agent that touches that data through a governed Snowflake gateway deepens the platform's gravitational pull. As Constellation Research analyst Michael Ni put it when the Natoma deal was announced, in comments reported by CIO.com: data platforms won the analytics era, and whoever governs agents, context, and autonomous actions wins the agentic one. A Forbes analysis of the same acquisition flagged the tension directly, noting that a governance layer living inside Snowflake risks pulling MCP's openness back toward a single vendor's control plane — attractive for Snowflake-standardized shops, more awkward for genuinely multi-vendor agent stacks. ... The urgency behind today’s announcement is not manufactured. Gartner predicts that by 2027, governance gaps discovered only after production incidents will force 40% of enterprises to demote or decommission autonomous AI agents — with analysts there warning that the greatest risk an agent poses often lies not in its output but in the actions it is empowered to take. IDC, meanwhile, expects more than 1 billion actively deployed AI agents by 2029, executing roughly 217 billion actions per day, and forecasts agentic AI will exceed $1.3 trillion in worldwide IT spending that year. The research firm's analysts now argue agentic platforms should be treated as decision infrastructure, not productivity software. Against that backdrop, the identity layer is becoming the contested ground, and every major vendor — Salesforce, ServiceNow, Microsoft, Google, Okta — is racing toward the same runtime-governance chokepoint. Snowflake's differentiator is proximity to the data itself. As Upadhyay put it, security "can't just be an API proxy sitting in front of an LLM. It has to anchor all the way down into the underlying data layer, enforcing zero-copy boundaries, dynamic data masking, and real-time exfiltration safeguards before an agent ever touches a row of data." The rollout now moves to proving ground. Cortex AI Gateway enters public preview soon, and the five partner integrations enter private preview, a phase Wang described as a deliberate feedback loop — customers on day one get an agent-access broker plus "a full audit log that will show you, for example, what that agent is actually doing," even when an agent deviates from its intent. Gnanasambandam, characteristically, wants enterprises to skip the easy demos entirely, urging customers to bring loan-origination workflows spanning three clouds and ten applications, half of them mainframes: "Give us that complex use case and bring anyone on and do it in your context, and we will take the challenge with anyone in the world."

headline: Snowflake Expands AWS Collaboration with $6B Commitment to Accelerate Enterprise Agentic AI Adoption
summary_text: - Multi-year strategic agreement expands joint investments in customer success, workload migrations, and go-to-market, as Snowflake surpasses $7 billion in lifetime AWS Marketplace sales - Snowflake commits $6 billion in Graviton compute and AI spend on AWS over five years, reflecting accelerating demand for data and AI workloads - Customers like Fetch and Hex are deploying AI applications on governed data with Snowflake on AWS Dubai, UAE — July 13, 2026 — Snowflake (NYSE: SNOW), the AI Data Cloud company, today announced that it has signed a multi-year strategic collaboration agreement (SCA) with Amazon Web Services (AWS) to accelerate enterprise agentic AI adoption to help joint customers worldwide build and deploy AI faster and more securely. As part of the expanded collaboration, Snowflake is making a $6 billion multi-year infrastructure commitment to AWS, its largest to date, reflecting the accelerating enterprise demand for AI and data workloads running on AWS. Snowflake was founded on AWS eleven years ago, and that foundation has grown into one of enterprise software’s broadest and deepest collaborations. The majority of Snowflake’s customers run on AWS today, with AWS recognizing Snowflake as a leading partner driving global customer adoption.The latest agreement builds on this momentum with deeper product integrations across generative AI and agentic AI, expanded go-to-market through AWS Marketplace, and joint investments in customer success programs, workload migrations, and strategic industry solutions designed to help enterprises move from AI experimentation to production-scale outcomes. ... Snowflake Cortex AI enables customers to build and deploy AI applications for text-to-SQL, summarization, sentiment analysis, and entity extraction directly within their Snowflake environment. Enterprises are rapidly adopting these capabilities to run AI on trusted, governed data without moving it outside their secure perimeter. Snowflake leverages AWS Graviton processors, delivering significant price-performance improvements for customers, and utilizing high performance, GPU-accelerated Amazon EC2 instances for AI model training and inference. Accelerating AI Adoption with AWS Since Snowflake first became available in AWS Marketplace, customers have embraced it as the fastest path to procure and deploy Snowflake’s AI and data capabilities – surpassing $7 billion in lifetime sales and exceeding $2 billion in calendar year sales in 2025, more than doubling transaction growth year-over-year. The expanded SCA builds on that trajectory, scaling joint initiatives to help even more customers discover, procure, and deploy AI and data solutions through AWS Marketplace with simplified contracting, faster procurement. Snowflake has also continued expanding its global footprint on AWS, with launches completed or underway in 10 new regions including New Zealand (Auckland), South Africa (Cape Town), Thailand (Bangkok), AWS European Sovereign Cloud, and others to help customers meet data residency requirements and deploy AI closer to where their business operates. Customers Deploying AI on Governed Data From startups to global enterprises, customers including Fetch and Hex use Snowflake on AWS to unify data, eliminate silos, and deploy AI applications and agents on governed data to drive measurable business impact.

headline: Haier Egypt plans expansion, eyes higher local production - Egyptian Gazette

headline: Haier’s smart home thinks, learns and acts. Even with robots - Il Sole 24 ORE
summary_text: BERLIN – Once again, the IFA trade fair provides Haier with the perfect opportunity to reaffirm two of its key strengths: its status as a leading player in the consumer electronics sector and its strong focus on sponsoring major sporting events to boost its brand visibility. In Berlin, the Chinese firm has been confirmed as the world leader in the large white goods sector for the 17th consecutive year and has announced an agreement signed with UEFA and the European Football Clubs Association to become, from 2027 (and for the next four years) a Global Partner of the UEFA Champions League. Significant focus is therefore placed on the brand, but also on a vision of the smart home that goes beyond simply adding a new smart function to a household appliance. The new frontier is ensuring that the home learns to understand what is happening within it and can intervene, when necessary, without waiting for the user to issue a single command or configure a specific mode of use for the device. Haier Europe’s slogan at Messe Berlin, ‘Home of Intelligent Possibilities’, can therefore be interpreted as a transition from a merely connected home to an ecosystem capable of interpreting its context, learning from the habits of those living within it, and coordinating the products and services that characterise their daily lives. The artificial intelligence integrated into various appliances (from washing machines to televisions) functions in this regard as a cross-cutting infrastructure spanning research and development, design (based on consumer scenarios and needs), production, user experience and after-sales services. The ultimate goal? To make technology increasingly invisible and capable of adapting to real-life situations, whilst leaving control in the hands of the user. ... In the new product announcements made in Berlin, the concepts of ‘new intelligence’ are being put into practice across all segments. In the washing cycle, for example, the Vision 15 uses a camera built into the washing machine door to monitor the load and recognise the quantity of laundry, colours, suds and any items that may have been left in the drum. Sensors and algorithms (AI Power Sense and AI Vision Sense) detect, interpret and process information relating to weight, balance, water level and temperature to automatically set various cycle parameters. As Haier’s managers explain, this technological innovation therefore operates ‘behind the scenes’, and the same applies to kitchen appliances. The AI Food Care System integrated into fridges is able to recognise food and suggest how to store it; the AI Vision system fitted to the ID Ultimate Series 6 ovens does the same with food to monitor the entire cooking cycle, automatically stopping the programme when the set result is achieved. Induction hobs and cooker hoods are also becoming increasingly intelligent: the former can transfer a pan’s cooking settings when it is moved (by detecting its position), whilst the latter can be activated simply with a gesture thanks to the MotionSense function. The digital backbone of the entire ecosystem is hOn, the app-based platform through which Haier manages products and services remotely within a single environment to intelligently optimise energy consumption. In this regard, as explained by Haier Europe’s CEO, Neil Tunstall, the Chinese company is set to invest 13 billion euros over the next five years in AI and IoT technologies, with the aim of bringing distributed intelligence into homes and introducing appliances capable not only of seeing, recognising and making decisions, but also of interacting with machines (robots) capable of physically acting within the home environment. ... of Haier’s technology in the field of laundry, the most ‘eye-catching’ new product showcased at IFA is the Multi Care Collection, a range of appliances designed to meet the need to run cycles with different loads simultaneously, thereby increasing flexibility in the home. The Multi Care Laundry Studio is, in fact, a product featuring four independent drums – one for the 10 kg washing machine, two 1 kg drums and one for the 8 kg tumble dryer – allowing each compartment to be managed separately, so that items differing in quantity, fabric or colour can be washed together. In the refrigeration sector, the Horizon Collection brings AI to the day-to-day management of food: the Hydro ... Having entered the Italian TV market just over a year ago, Haier is now seeking to take a step forward in terms of technology by effectively adopting the same architecture used for the company’s other products. At the heart of the new range of smart TVs is UltraSense AI, a platform based on a proprietary processor that continuously analyses images and sound and adjusts the TV’s settings in real time according to the content and environmental conditions. The artificial intelligence operates on four levels. AI Cinema recognises the characteristics of individual scenes and optimises colour, contrast, depth, HDR, definition and the smoothness of movement. AI Sound, on the other hand, works on voice separation, frequency balancing and volume to make dialogue clearer and the soundscape more uniform (on some models, the audio is handled by Sound by KEF, the historic British brand). For those using the television with a games console or a PC, AI Game works to reduce input lag, screen tearing and interruptions. Finally, AI Eye Caring adjusts brightness and contrast to suit ambient lighting conditions and the content to enhance viewing comfort. The range features various panel technologies, from QD-Mini LED to OLED, with screen sizes up to 115 inches. Whilst the spectacular innovation showcased at IFA is an impressive 163-inch Micro LED screen (created by combining multiple panels), the manufacturer’s decision to pair LED backlighting with technologies such as the Pure RGB Light Engine (in the new MR92 series from 55 inches upwards) and Super Quantum Dot Colour (on the new MS 96 range from 100 inches) – which work on the three primary colour components and the colour spectrum in combination with AI algorithms that reduce interference between the different channels. The aim is clear: to achieve better visual performance and to try to narrow the gap with those who currently dominate the world of television. ... The real big news (in terms of future prospects) that the Chinese company unveiled at IFA comes, however, from the field of robotics, The humanoid robots on display at Haier’s stand – capable of perceiving their surroundings and acting within them, interacting with people and household appliances – are perhaps the most striking expression of the ‘Home of Intelligent Possibilities’ vision. We’re talking about systems that load and unload the washing and organise food in the fridge, which recognise and categorise items to be cleaned, distinguishing between different types of dirt and deciding what action to take. These are companion robots that provide personal assistance through voice interaction (in Italia, a connection with smartwatches is currently being developed) in everyday activities. Intelligence is therefore not confined to software but takes shape in a physical body (‘embodied intelligence’), such as that of the W3 Exoskeleton, a carbon and titanium alloy exoskeleton that uses sensors and AI algorithms to reduce physical effort, interpreting the wearer’s movement intentions in real time and automatically adjusting the level of assistance based on their characteristics and the activity being performed. This trial, which for the time being is focused solely on the Chinese market, confirms a very specific line of thinking: the smart, connected home of tomorrow, according to Haier, will go beyond the ability of a single appliance to self-regulate and will become a system distributed across multiple devices that will require fewer and fewer instructions and offer ever greater autonomy.

headline: Avantium partners with Klöckner Pentaplast to advance PEF food packaging
summary_text: - Avantium has signed a capacity reservation agreement with kp films to explore the use of the plant-based PEF polymer releaf in thermoformed food packaging. - Releaf PEF offers enhanced oxygen and carbon dioxide barrier properties compared with PET, with potential benefits including extended shelf life, cutting food waste, and lightweighting. - The agreement supports Avantium’s plans to scale FDCA and PEF production through licensed industrial plants, following progress at its FDCA Flagship Plant in the Netherlands. Avantium has signed a capacity reservation agreement with Klöckner Pentaplast (kp films). The agreement allows the companies to explore the commercialization of Avantium’s plant-based polymer PE furanoate (PEF), branded as releaf. The solution, made from furandicarboxylic acid (FDCA), can be used in thermoformed food packaging, including trays and other packaging designed to protect fresh and prepared foods. ... The move comes after Avantium signed a capacity reservation agreement with Logoplaste Consultores Técnicos and a memorandum of understanding with Tereos and Louis Vuitton Moët Hennessy last year to accelerate the industrial-scale production releaf. ... Looking ahead, the capacity reservation agreement supports kp films’ access to future volumes of releaf from prospective industrial-scale plants to be built and operated by licensees using Avantium’s technology. The agreement aims to support commercial deployment of releaf in thermoformed food packaging applications across Europe, and aligns with Avantium’s strategy to establish a global network of licensed PEF production facilities. “Avantium is currently reaching an important commercial milestone with the start-up of its FDCA Flagship Plant in Delfzijl, the Netherlands. All major process units have been successfully commissioned, and during the remainder of 2026, the company is focused on completing plant start-up, producing the first FDCA batches, and beginning its first commercial shipments by the end of the year,” shares Van Reedt Dortland. The start of the plant was previously delayed due to construction-related issues, expected to cost an additional €7 million (US$7.6 million) in capital expenditure. “The Flagship Plant is the foundation of Avantium’s licensing-led growth strategy. Rather than building and financing every future production facility itself, Avantium intends to license its YXY Technology to industrial partners that will build and operate larger FDCA plants. The plant serves as the commercial-scale reference for these future licensees, providing operational experience, product validation, and production data.” Van Reedt Dortland tells us that commercial interest in the technology is increasing. Avantium has signed 23 offtake agreements for FDCA/PEF volumes from the FDCA Flagship Plant and secured more than 150,000 metric tons per annum of capacity reservations for volumes produced in future licensed plants. “Avantium is also building a resilient supply chain through a flexible feedstock strategy. The company’s current process uses plant-based sugars derived from abundant agricultural co-products (high fructose syrup), while ongoing technology development is focused on expanding future feedstock options,” she says.
