Zeta Global Holdings Corp. has authorized the issuance of up to $25 million of its Class A common stock, a move that will be executed over the next several fiscal quarters as non‑cash consideration for services rendered by a specific provider. The authorization is contained in a prospectus supplement filed on September 11, 2026, and is not a traditional public equity offering aimed at raising cash for general corporate purposes. Under the terms of the supplement, the shares will be issued in tranches that align with the completion of agreed‑upon service milestones. The maximum number of shares that could be issued, based on an illustrative price of $30.56 per share—the last reported sale price on September 10, 2026—would bring the total Class A shares outstanding to roughly 227.5 million. headline: ZetaTech Appoints NanoViz as Technology Commercialisation Partner for ZECOA™
summary_text: We are pleased to announce that ZetaTech Sdn. Bhd. has appointed NanoViz Group Sdn. Bhd. as its Technology Commercialisation Partner for ZECOA™, its carbon-capture nano-additive technology. The appointment marks an important transition for ZECOA™, from technology development towards structured commercialisation and global market engagement. Under the appointment, NanoViz will promote and market ZECOA™, develop customers, manufacturers and strategic partners, coordinate application qualification and Joint Development Programmes (JDPs), and support licensing and deployment. Importantly, ZECOA™ is not beginning its commercialisation journey purely as a laboratory technology. headline: The Label Rollup Story That Almost Repeated Itself | AInvest
summary_text: - Affix Holdings merged three label companies under a private equity model avoiding high leverage, contrasting with Multi-Color's $5.9B debt-driven collapse in 2026. - Portrait Capital's strategy prioritizes small, founder-led acquisitions with operational independence, emphasizing patience over aggressive growth. - The $49B label market faces RFID adoption and digital printing growth, but Multi-Color's failure shows leverage risks outweigh market tailwinds. - Investors must assess whether Affix's restrained approach creates resilience or merely delays pressure to scale, as industry consolidation nears 80% by 2027. Affix Holdings announced its formation today by combining three label companies into one platform. It's a private company, not a stock you can buy. But the announcement is worth reading — because it tells a story about private equity, leverage, and what happens to a rollup strategy when the debt it runs on stops flowing. ... labels for safety compliance, product identification ... For most of the past decade, ... 's exactly what ... . Private equity firms built label platforms, bought add-on companies, and used debt to fund the acquisitions. The industry had 40 deals in 2021, 49 in 2022. The model worked — until the ... stopped working. Multi-Color Corporation, one of the biggest label companies in the world, filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in January 2026. It was owned by private equity firm Clayton, Dubilier & Rice. Multi-Color operated in 25 countries with more than 90 facilities and employed 12,800 people. At the time it filed, it carried $5.9 billion in debt. Its revenue fell from $3.56 billion in 2022 to $3.06 billion in 2025. EBITDA dropped from $598 million to $409 million. Existing equity holders — the PE sponsors — saw their positions wiped to zero. Multi-Color didn't fail ... being useful. The end markets were fine. It failed because the leverage structure that built it couldn't survive when revenue normalized, costs rose, and the company was slow to adjust pricing. Affix is built by the same kind of capital, but with a different shape. Portrait Capital, a private investment firm founded in 2022, acquired AAi Labels — a company founded in 1969 and run by the same family since 1998 — along with Sticker Ranch, a digital-first web-to-print label operation. In July 2026, AAi acquired Guaranteed Labels, a custom label manufacturer in Alabama founded in 1988. Today's announcement wraps all three under the Affix Holdings name. The companies remain independent in operation. Lynn Higgs, who co-founded Sticker Ranch, runs the platform. Portrait Capital describes itself as crafting transitions for founders and family business owners. Its website shows investments in a durable label manufacturer, a tire recycling company, a water service provider, and an agricultural brokerage — all small, regional, founder-led businesses. This is a different rhythm from the Multi-Color model. Portrait Capital isn't racing to build a global platform. It's making deliberate acquisitions of small, established companies and keeping their operators involved. The strategy is patient rather than aggressive. ... Portrait Capital hasn't disclosed financial terms for any of its three acquisitions. The combined revenue of the three companies is unknown. We don't know how much debt backs the platform, if any. The fact that nothing has been published says something: this isn't a company trying to impress anyone with its size. Compare that to the peak rollup era. Companies like Multi-Color competed in auctions, paying high multiples for add-on targets, funded by increasingly aggressive debt structures. The pressure to keep buying, to keep growing, to justify the premium — that's what drove the expansion. And when the environment shifted, the same pressure made retrenchment impossible. Affix's model may avoid that trap simply because it doesn't start with the same urgency. Three small companies, each running independently, with a clear path to add more without needing to prove something to a wall street audience. The smaller scale is a constraint — it means less immediate impact and a longer time horizon. But it also means less structural risk. The label market gives some comfort. The global label market was valued at roughly $49 billion in 2026, growing at about 5% per year. RFID adoption is accelerating — major retailers like Walmart and Kroger are pushing traceability initiatives, and the FDA extended compliance deadlines to 2028. That creates demand for converters who can handle RFID-capable labels. Digital printing is expanding the range of short-run, custom work that small converters can profitably handle. But market growth doesn't protect a company from its own capital structure. Multi-Color saw the same tailwinds and still collapsed under its debt. Here's what to watch for as an investor evaluating this kind of story — not just in labels, but in any industry where private equity is buying small businesses and combining them. The rollup strategy is attractive until you test whether it scales without breaking. The test isn't how many acquisitions a company makes. It's whether the company can survive a bad year. Multi-Color couldn't survive a 14% revenue decline. The debt structure was the problem. The business wasn't. Portrait Capital seems aware of this. Their investment philosophy explicitly targets founder-led businesses and emphasizes honoring the legacy of the existing operators. Whether that translates into a more resilient platform depends on whether restraint is built into the strategy or whether it's just the first phase before the pressure to grow kicks in. The label consolidation wave isn't over. Industry analysts project it could reach 80% penetration by 2027. There are still plenty of small companies to buy. The question for anyone watching this space is whether the next Affix will be the next Multi-Color in disguise, or whether there's a genuine alternative to the high-leverage model that just failed. The answer won't come from a press release. It'll come from whether the company can grow without borrowing more than it can repay when things go wrong.

headline: KDV Label Opens New Waukesha Manufacturing Plant
summary_text: # KDV Label Cuts Ribbon on 117,000-Square-Foot Waukesha Plant, Eyes More Growth ... KDV Label has opened the doors on a sprawling new 117,000-square-foot manufacturing facility near Les Paul Parkway in Waukesha, consolidating what had been scattered local operations under a single roof built with room to grow even bigger down the line. The custom label manufacturer marked the occasion with a grand-opening event on August 5, welcoming customers, business partners, suppliers, and community members to tour the new building and watch live demonstrations of its label-printing capabilities. The facility sits at 2230 Corporate Drive and was designed and built by Brookfield-based Briohn Building Corporation, which broke ground on the site in May 2025, according to KDV Label. As reported by Greater Milwaukee Today, KDV Label President and CEO Keith Walz noted the company broke ground on the site roughly a year before opening it, and that the new plant includes manufacturing space, printing presses, offices, and warehousing all in one location. The site was engineered with room for a future 39,000-square-foot addition, giving the company a clear runway for further expansion. ... KDV Label expects that bringing its Waukesha operations together under one roof will make it easier for teams to collaborate and improve the flow of materials and work through the plant, per the same account. The company manufactures custom labels for the food, beverage, personal care, dairy, automotive, and specialty consumer goods industries, and the new operation is built to support pressure-sensitive and digital labels, expanded content labels, unsupported film labels, variable data labels, and promotional labels. Walz said the facility reflects the company's commitment and positions it to keep delivering service, quality, and partnership to customers, according to a company news release cited by Greater Milwaukee Today. The expanded facility provides additional production capacity at a moment when demand for custom labels is increasing, the outlet reports. KDV Label said the investment will help the company respond to that growing customer demand while preserving the quality and attention to detail associated with its products. The expansion also includes investment in label-printing technology, workforce development, and relationships with customers and suppliers. ... The Waukesha site includes a dedicated digital print room three times larger than KDV's previous digital print area, a technology upgrade that enables faster turnarounds for high-SKU consumer packaging, according to Packaging Impressions. That kind of flexible, short-run digital capability has become increasingly important to consumer packaged goods brands. Job postings from May indicate KDV Label was actively recruiting flexographic press operators, digital press operators, and press helpers across second and third shifts to staff the new plant. The grand-opening event featured demonstrations of technology supporting KDV's continued growth, and a photograph provided by the City of Waukesha shows Walz holding scissors alongside Waukesha Mayor Alicia Halvensleben at the ribbon-cutting. KDV Label was founded in 1974 by Karen and Dick Vaughn in a family garage and was later expanded four-fold under second-generation leader Shane Vaughn, who served as CEO for 27 years before retiring in April 2023. Keith Walz took over as president and CEO that same month after serving as chief financial officer since 2021, bringing prior executive experience from Brady Corporation and Osborn LLC. ... headline: Sanofi and Cheplapharm to create new strategic partnership in mature medicines
summary_text: Sanofi and Cheplapharm, a European leader in well-established medicines, announced their intention to create a strategic partnership under which Cheplapharm would take over from Sanofi a selection of 20 mature medicines and three manufacturing sites worldwide. In return, Sanofi will receive a 26.4% equity stake in Cheplapharm, building on a collaboration that started in 2014. The partnership is based on a shared conviction: that innovative medicines and certain mature medicines have different needs and should benefit from operating models tailored to their specific manufacturing, regulatory and commercial requirements. Cheplapharm's specialized expertise will ensure these medicines continue to meet patients' needs throughout the next stage of their lifecycle. "Our multi-year journey to simplify our mature portfolio has enabled us to focus on innovation while ensuring mature medicines continue to reach patients who need them. Cheplapharm has been a trusted partner for more than a decade and this transaction significantly builds on its prior acquisitions from Sanofi's mature medicines portfolio. This new partnership, together with our equity stake in Cheplapharm, underscores our commitment to ensuring patients continue to benefit from today’s essential medicines while also pursuing tomorrow’s breakthroughs," said Thomas Grenier, Executive Vice President, General Medicines, Sanofi. "This partnership marks a major milestone for Cheplapharm. Through this project, we are incorporating products that complement our extensive portfolio, as well as the expertise and manufacturing capabilities required to produce a flagship product, Lovenox®/Clexane®. This represents a long-term pharmaceutical and industrial commitment: to invest in our sites and their expertise, to preserve rare skills, and to ensure the long-term availability of these treatments for patients." "We are proud to pursue this ambition alongside Sanofi," said Edeltraud Lafer and Sebastian Braun, both Co-CEOs of Cheplapharm. As part of the project, three manufacturing sites would be transferred to Cheplapharm: Csanyikvölgy in Hungary (c.400 employees), Jurong in Singapore (c.100 employees), and Ploërmel in France (c.65 employees). The teams would continue their activities with existing employment arrangements and collective agreements maintained. Sanofi and Cheplapharm will work closely together to ensure a smooth transition and continuity of supply in compliance with the highest manufacturing quality standards. The commercial transfer of the medicine portfolio is planned to begin in the first quarter of 2027, followed by the transfer of the sites, subject to employee information and consultation procedures with employee representatives, regulatory approvals and customary closing conditions. The transaction is expected to be fully completed by the third quarter of 2027. For Cheplapharm, this partnership represents an important step ensuring the continuity of its strategic growth. For Sanofi, it will enable the company to continue focusing its efforts on innovation, while supporting certain established medicines through the next stage of their lifecycle. Financial considerations for Sanofi The proposed transaction is not expected to have any impact on Sanofi’s financial guidance for 2026. The medicines being divested from Sanofi include Lovenox/Clexane (enoxaparin)(1). Additional financial details are expected to be provided at a later stage. ... Driven by a long-term vision of sustainable growth, the Group has invested more than €6.2 billion since its inception, acquired nearly 100 products since 2015, and holds 3,440 marketing authorizations across 160 countries. Cheplapharm is the market leader in France and a leading European player in this market segment.

summary_text: CHS, OCP North America Launch Major Initiative To Strengthen U.S. Fertilizer Supply Anticipated up to $450 million investment expected to improve supply reliability for American farmers | Potato Grower Magazine ... CHS, America’s leading farmer-owned cooperative, and OCP North America, a subsidiary of the OCP Group, are taking a major step to strengthen domestic fertilizer production in the United States. Through a proposed joint venture, the two companies are preparing to build and operate a phosphate fertilizer production facility at the Cornerstone Energy Park located in Waggaman, Louisiana. The new plant is expected to produce over 1 million metric tonnes of phosphate-based fertilizer annually and would be the first of its kind constructed in the United States since 1984. American farmers use phosphate fertilizer to grow the crops that fuel and feed the world. However, phosphate reserves in the country are declining and today the U.S. imports approximately 40 percent of the phosphate-based fertilizer that is used to meet farmer demand. The potential to bring this new capacity online could reduce U.S. dependency on imported phosphate-based fertilizer by more than 48 percent, significantly strengthening the domestic fertilizer supply chain. “This is an exciting moment for American agriculture,” said Jay Debertin, president and CEO of CHS. “As a farmer-owned cooperative, we exist to help farmers succeed. Together with OCP North America, we have the opportunity to build the first phosphate fertilizer plant in the U.S. in more than 40 years. This investment has the potential to create more value for our owners by bringing fertilizer production closer to the American farmer and the cooperative network.” In connection with the proposed joint venture, the OCP Group will supply phosphoric acid to the facility, drawing on its global phosphate expertise and resources. Finished fertilizer products will be distributed through both OCP North America and CHS, which serves cooperatives, retailers and farmers across the United States through its extensive wholesale and retail crop nutrients network. The new fertilizer plant’s expected location within the Cornerstone Energy Park in Waggaman helps ensure access to raw materials and the ability to transport products via the Mississippi River system. "This project represents a milestone in OCP North America’s commitment to serving American agriculture,” said Kevin Kimm, CEO of OCP North America. “Together with CHS, we aim to build lasting infrastructure that strengthens U.S. food security and delivers a reliable, domestically produced supply of the crop nutrients American farmers need.” Once approved, the project is expected to create approximately 60 permanent, high impact jobs in Jefferson Parish along with 500 construction jobs. The parties estimate that the project will have a total job impact of 924 direct and services-support jobs. This is expected to bring real, positive economic and community impact to the state of Louisiana. headline: LEAP India’s IPO signals momentum in India’s logistics and supply chain sector
summary_text: LEAP India Limited, the country's largest on-demand asset pooling platform, has successfully launched an INR 24.8 billion initial public offering (IPO) on the National Stock Exchange of India and BSE Limited. This transaction highlights the growing investor interest in businesses that enhance supply chain efficiency and reflects the increasing maturity of India's capital markets. For the logistics sector, the move underscores the scalability of asset-pooling models and the strategic importance of material handling equipment in modernizing regional trade infrastructure. LEAP India Limited, a portfolio company of global investment firm KKR, completed its INR 24.8 billion IPO through a combination of a fresh equity issue and an offer for sale by existing shareholders. Major sellers included Vertical Holdings II Pte. Ltd, which is controlled by KKR, and the KIA EBT Scheme 3. The offering was conducted under Rule 144A and Regulation S, targeting both domestic and international investors. A&O Shearman served as the sole international legal counsel for the underwriters, managing the offering structure and ensuring compliance with international securities laws. As India's leading on-demand asset pooling provider, LEAP India specializes in supplying pallets, containers, and various material handling equipment to a diverse range of industrial clients. The IPO process was notably complex due to the company's acquisition of CHEP India in early 2025. To account for this major expansion, the draft red herring prospectus required the inclusion of pro forma financial statements, providing a comprehensive view of the merged entity's financial health and operational scale within the supply chain management market. The successful listing is viewed by industry experts as a bellwether for the logistics and supply chain sector in India. Partner Pallavi Gopinath Aney noted that the transaction reflects strong sector momentum and the ability to navigate intricate cross-border regulatory and disclosure requirements. By securing significant capital, LEAP India is positioned to further optimize supply chain efficiencies, signaling to the broader market that logistics infrastructure and asset management are becoming increasingly attractive to global private capital and public market investors.

headline: CHEP Owner Brambles Lifts Annual Profit 4% Despite Repair Constraints -- Update | MarketScreener Hong Kong
summary_text: # CHEP Owner Brambles Lifts Annual Profit ... % Despite Repair ... -- Update Published on 08/20 ... 2026 at 05:56 am HKT Dow Jones BRAMBLES LIMITED By Stuart Condie SYDNEY--Global pallet supplier Brambles reported a 4% rise in annual profit, meeting its downgraded guidance despite a larger-than-expected financial hit from the U.S. repair constraints that prompted a historic selloff of its stock. Australia-listed Brambles, which leases out pallets under the CHEP brand, on Thursday reported an annual underlying profit of $1.49 billion, up by 4% on the prior year once currency moves were stripped out. Sales revenue for the 12 months through June rose by 2% to $7.04 billion, also on a constant-currency basis. Brambles had initially guided for an 8% to 11% rise in underlying profit, but slashed its outlook in May to between 3% and 5% on an increase in costs from unexpected capacity constraints at subcontracted pallet service centers in parts of the U.S. The downgrade prompted the stock's largest one-day drop since 2002. Several formerly bullish analysts cut their rating and the consensus forecast for annual underlying profit fell from $1.565 billion to $1.48 billion ahead of Thursday's result announcement. Analysts had been looking for sales of $7.04 billion, according to data compiled by Visible Alpha. Brambles said its underlying profit had taken a $90 million hit from the U.S. repair constraints, exceeding its prior estimate by 50%. The effect included lost revenue and additional transport and plant costs, it said. More positively, additional fourth-quarter pallet purchases to address shortages cost $40 million, $20 million less than expected, as it utilized excess pallets in storage. Brambles, which raised its dividend to $0.2315 from $0.2083, said it expected to resolve the constraint issues by the end of December, as previously flagged. "Our actions are already delivering positive results, with customer order fulfilment improving materially since mid April," Chief Executive Graham Chipchase said. "We remain on track to resolve the repair capacity constraints by the end of the first half of FY27 and position our U.S. business to strengthen customer relationships and pursue growth." Payment for the new pallets is due in the December half and Brambles expects to spend another $60 million on an additional 2 million new pallets in the same period, resulting in a total cash outflow of $100 million. Brambles expects fiscal 2027 free cash flow before dividends of between $800 million and $950 million, down from $1.05 billion in the fiscal year just ended. It expects underlying profit growth of between 2% and 6%, and sales revenue growth of between 2% and 4%, both in constant currency terms. Brambles didn't add to the $400 million buyback extension announced in May. It expects to complete the current on-market buyback in the current fiscal year. headline: Tinicum Acquires Aerospace Chemicals Distributor GracoRoberts
summary_text: Tinicum Acquires Aerospace Chemicals Distributor GracoRoberts ... ## The GracoRoberts management team retains a significant stake and continues to lead the business, ending an 11-year ownership by CM Equity Partners GracoRoberts supplies the adhesives, sealants, coatings, composites, and other specialty chemicals that aircraft and defense manufacturers use to build and maintain their products. July 28, 2026| John ... Tinicum has acquired GracoRoberts, a distributor of specialty chemicals and composites used in the aerospace and defense industry, from CM Equity Partners. GracoRoberts supplies the adhesives, sealants, coatings, composites, and other specialty chemicals that aircraft and defense manufacturers use to build and maintain their products. The company sells through an omnichannel model, combining an eCommerce operation with a technical sales team that helps customers select and apply the right materials. GracoRoberts is certified to the aerospace industry’s AS and ISO quality standards and to the Department of Defense’s CMMC Level II cybersecurity standard, and it is authorized to distribute more than 50 specialty chemical brands, including 3M, AkzoNobel, Eastman, ExxonMobil, Henkel, Hexcel, Huntsman, Momentive, and Resin Formulators. Beyond distribution, GracoRoberts runs a defense logistics and compliance program that manages the supply chain for military operations end to end, and it offers services such as custom kitting, labeling, repackaging, cold storage, and vendor-managed inventory. The business is made up of parent GracoRoberts together with Silmid, SkyGeek, Pacific Coast Composites, and Sky Mart, and it operates an on-site, staffed chemical laboratory and testing facility. Arlington, Texas-headquartered GracoRoberts is led by chief executive officer Jason Caldwell. CM Equity acquired Graco Supply in September 2015 and has spent the past 11 years growing the business through a series of acquisitions that added California-based E.V. Roberts (May 2019) — the merger that produced the GracoRoberts name — UK-based Silmid (March 2021); New York-based SkyGeek (July 2022); Washington-based Pacific Coast Composites (May 2023); and Florida-based Sky Mart (January 2026). ... “Tinicum shares our commitment to our people, our partners, and the long-term success of this business,” said Mr. Caldwell. “This partnership provides additional resources to invest in our team, strengthen our capabilities, and continue delivering exceptional value to the customer and supplier partners we serve. We are incredibly proud of what our employees have built over the past decade alongside financial partner CM Equity, and we are excited to build on that foundation in this next chapter of growth.” “It has been a privilege to partner with the GracoRoberts management team over the past 11 years,” said Jeffrey Mark, a managing partner at CM Equity. “Working together, we executed a value creation strategy centered on strategic acquisitions, operational excellence, and sustained organic growth, transforming GracoRoberts into the market-leading company it is today. We are proud of what the team has accomplished and believe the company is exceptionally well positioned for continued success with Tinicum.” ... “We greatly admire the business that the GracoRoberts team has built. It is distinguished by the team’s technical depth, unwavering commitment to customer service, and longstanding partnerships with the world’s leading material manufacturers,” said Erik Blumenkranz, a partner at Tinicum. “We intend to invest behind that foundation with a long-term mindset — in the people, the capabilities, and the platform,” added Roddy Cruz, a partner at Tinicum. “It is exactly the kind of durable, market-leading business we seek to partner with.” The buy of GracoRoberts lands in a corner of the aerospace supply chain buoyed by rising defense budgets and a busy aftermarket. The US aerospace adhesives and sealants market was worth roughly $360 million in 2025 and is expected to grow at about 5.7% a year through 2035, according to Precedence Research, while global estimates for 2026 range between $1.2 billion and $1.5 billion across research firms. North America accounts for more than 40% of volume, a lead that traces to sustained US military spending and the contractors and distributors that supply it. Demand is driven by the move to lightweight composite airframes, which rely on bonded rather than fastened joints, and by a maintenance, repair, and overhaul cycle that keeps specialty chemicals moving long after an aircraft is delivered. Distributors that pair technical support with compliance and logistics, as GracoRoberts does, sit at the center of that flow. For Tinicum, the appeal is a distributor with defensible characteristics: certifications and compliance standards that are difficult for new entrants to clear, deep technical relationships with both suppliers and aerospace customers, and a recurring aftermarket revenue base. The firm has signaled a long-hold approach rather than a quick flip, planning to invest behind the platform’s people and capabilities and to keep the management team in place with a meaningful equity stake. That continuity, paired with additional capital for acquisitions and internal investment, positions GracoRoberts to extend the buy-and-build strategy CM Equity began — consolidating a fragmented supply chain for specialty aerospace chemicals while deepening its position with blue-chip material manufacturers.

headline: Tricon Energy: The Chemical Trader Betting on Full Ownership
summary_text: Tricon Energy made the 2026 MDM Top Distributors lists in Plastics and Lubricants & Fuels. Here's the take-title trading model behind its $14B climb. Tricon Energy lands on two of Modern Distribution Management's 2026 Top Distributors lists, Plastics and Lubricants & Fuels, with $14.0 billion in revenue per MDM's report. That places a Houston commodities house founded by a Barcelona-born trader with four employees and a phone line ahead of most household-name industrial distributors on the same list. The story of how it got there runs through a decision most of its peers made in the opposite direction. ... Ignacio Torras founded Tricon in Houston in 1996, trading liquid caustic soda and acetone with a handful of colleagues. The company opened its first overseas office in Korea in 1999, in the middle of the Asian financial crisis, then added Shanghai and Istanbul in 2004. It crossed one million metric tons handled in 2002 and $1 billion in sales in 2006, the same year it launched Tricon Plastics. Tricon Dry Chemicals followed in 2008, and Liquid Fuels and Raw Materials units arrived between 2015 and 2017, per the company's own history page. By 2024 the firm was moving roughly 24 million tons of chemicals a year out of more than 28 offices in over 100 countries, according to Forbes. ICIS now ranks Tricon the second-largest chemical distributor in the world, behind only Germany's Brenntag. ... Chemical distribution has spent two decades drifting toward asset-light brokerage: take a fee, move title fast, keep inventory and price exposure off the balance sheet. Tricon runs the opposite playbook. Torras describes it to Forbes as the "Walmart of chemicals": the company buys commodity volumes outright, five thousand tons of polyethylene resin at a time, warehouses them in Houston or another hub, and carries the price and inventory risk itself before breaking the lot into smaller shipments, three hundred tons to Algeria, five hundred to Nigeria, sold to manufacturers who could never place an order at bulk scale. That is a real bet, not a slogan. Taking physical possession means Tricon eats commodity price swings, storage costs, and shipping risk that a pure broker would pass through. The payoff is a role brokers cannot fill: Tricon becomes the buffer between volatile bulk commodity markets and manufacturers who need reliable, right-sized supply regardless of what polyethylene or xylene did that week. It is also why the company needs serious balance sheet muscle. Tricon operates on roughly $2.7 billion in credit lines from banks including Societe Generale and Mitsui Marubeni, per Forbes, capital that funds inventory most of its lean, fee-based competitors never touch. ... That credit capacity does double duty as an acquisition engine, and Tricon has used it specifically during industry downturns rather than waiting for better conditions. Q-Logistics and Mexican polymer distributor Polymat joined in 2023, giving Tricon three terminal shipment centers and five-plus warehouses across Mexico, per the company's announcement. eXsource followed in 2024. In Africa, Tricon took an initial strategic stake in West African International Group in March 2025, then converted it to a full acquisition roughly a year later, a two-step structure the company's own release frames as validating the regional partnership before committing fully, per Tricon's announcement. Torras told Forbes that larger rival Brenntag "sees us in the rear view mirror" and is closing the gap. Buying distribution assets while competitors retrench is a strategy with an obvious trade-off: it works only if the balance sheet can absorb a downturn that runs longer or deeper than planned, and Tricon's entire model leans on the credit lines holding up through that stretch. ... The other quiet tension in Tricon's story is ownership structure. Brenntag, Univar, and most of the scaled chemical distributors are public companies or private-equity roll-ups answering to shareholders on quarterly cycles. Tricon, at $14 billion in revenue, remains privately held and founder-controlled, which is precisely what lets it fund inventory-heavy, countercyclical acquisitions on bank credit rather than managing to a stock price. Torras landed on the 2026 Forbes World Billionaires List with a $1.5 billion net worth, and the company was Forbes' highest-ranking newcomer on its 2025 Top Private Companies list at No. 35. Staying private at that scale, in a sector where nearly every serious competitor has gone public or been rolled up, is itself a strategic choice, one that trades access to public capital markets for the freedom to run a physical, capital-intensive trading book on its own timeline. Tricon also uses that trading flexibility defensively. When new tariffs hit specific import lanes, such as duties on Korean benzene, the company has substituted duty-free alternatives like acetone or styrene monomer that serve similar manufacturing purposes, insulating customers from a policy shock a pure broker would simply pass along, per Forbes. Internally, Torras leans on a blunt operating mantra employees call W2MTC, work two more hours than the competition, and frames the business in cyclical terms: day follows night, and the trader who prepares for the turn is the one still standing when it comes. For a company that has grown from four people trading caustic soda to a $14 billion operation spanning 28 offices, the discipline behind that line is doing more work than the slogan lets on.

headline: Tri Polarcon Strengthens Construction Chemicals Presence with Rockhard Acquisition | Chemical Industry Digest
summary_text: Tri Polarcon Pvt. Ltd., a Pune-based manufacturer and exporter of construction chemicals, acquired 100% ownership of Rockhard Polycoats Pvt. Ltd. The acquisition strengthens Tri Polarcon’s presence in India’s growing construction chemicals market, particularly in industrial flooring, protective coatings, waterproofing and structural repair solutions. Rockhard Polycoats, also based in the Pune region, brings specialised expertise in industrial epoxy flooring, PU flooring, protective coatings and structural repair. As a result, the acquisition enables Tri Polarcon to broaden its technical capabilities and offer a more comprehensive range of solutions to industrial and infrastructure customers. ... The two companies operate in complementary segments of the construction chemicals industry. Tri Polarcon markets its products under the TRIFLOR brand and manufactures a wide portfolio of epoxy, PU, EPU and water-based flooring systems. Its product range also includes waterproofing solutions, protective and anti-corrosive coatings, sealants, grouts, adhesives, mortars and concrete admixtures. Moreover, the company supports its offerings through in-house manufacturing and research and development capabilities. Rockhard Polycoats developed specialised expertise in industrial epoxy and PU flooring, protective coatings, antistatic flooring and car parking flooring. The company also undertakes structural repair, restoration and steel protection projects. Therefore, by bringing these complementary capabilities together, Tri Polarcon aims to strengthen its ability to serve customers requiring integrated construction chemical and flooring solutions. ... India’s construction chemicals sector continues to evolve as industrial facilities, warehouses, infrastructure projects, pharmaceutical plants and food-grade facilities become larger and more technically demanding. Consequently, customers increasingly require integrated solutions covering industrial flooring, waterproofing, protective coatings and structural repair instead of working with multiple specialised vendors. The acquisition positions Tri Polarcon to respond to this changing market requirement. By combining Rockhard Polycoats’ specialised site experience and established client relationships with Tri Polarcon’s broader product portfolio and manufacturing capabilities, the company expects to create stronger value for its customers. ... Vijay Mohite, Chief General Manager of Tri Polarcon, said, “I’ve spent more than twenty years in this industry, and I know a deal like this doesn’t mean much on its own. What matters is what we do with it — bringing two strong teams together and making sure customers actually feel the benefit.” Tri Polarcon has stated that it plans to build on Rockhard Polycoats’ existing technical capabilities and customer relationships rather than replace them. Accordingly, the company views the acquisition as the beginning of an integration process focused on strengthening capabilities and improving customer offerings. The company has not disclosed the transaction value, employee details or a specific integration timeline. ... The acquisition also reflects a broader trend of consolidation within India’s construction chemicals and coatings industry. As projects become increasingly complex, manufacturers are expanding their product portfolios and technical capabilities to offer more complete solutions across multiple applications. Companies with expertise in industrial flooring, waterproofing, protective coatings and structural repair are particularly well positioned to benefit from this growing demand for integrated solutions. ... With the acquisition of Rockhard Polycoats, Tri Polarcon takes another important step towards strengthening its position in India’s construction chemicals industry. The combined capabilities will enhance Tri Polarcon’s presence across industrial epoxy and PU flooring, waterproofing, protective coatings, structural repair and specialised construction chemical solutions. As per the press release, the acquisition could help the company serve increasingly complex industrial and infrastructure projects while building a stronger position in India’s evolving construction chemicals market. headline: SC cleaning products maker to add a new filling line
summary_text: A Lowcountry outsourcing manufacturer is investing $3.4 million to increase capacity. Walterboro-based Trison Wells LLC said last week that the expansion is expected to create 30 jobs at 1756 Industrial Road. The company is adding a new liquid-fill production line at its existing plant that “will significantly increase its annual … capacity,” according to a statement from the S.C. Commerce Department. Trison Wells is a full-service contract manufacturer. It formulates, makes and packages name-brand and private-label detergents and other cleaning products for customers in the laundry and household-, personal-, pet- and car-care industries. The company was a startup when it began production in Colleton County in mid-2022 with a $1.2 million investment that was to create 35 jobs. It took over an 82,000-square-foot building formerly occupied by Optimum Nutrition. On its website, Trison Wells stresses to U.S. cleaning product makers the benefits of “onshoring" and “nearshoring” their production work. “The old default of automatically going offshore for the lowest unit price no longer holds up to scrutiny, especially for heavy, repeat-purchase liquid cleaners in a world of tariffs and fragile freight,” according to a June 4 blog post. “The brands that win in 2026 are the ones making a deliberate, all-in decision about where their products are made, and that decision increasingly favors nearshore speed, control and resilience.” The company added that it provides “the best of that picture: fast, reliable domestic production anchored in South Carolina, backed by a nearshore network for scale.”

summary_text: With the rapid development and iteration of 5G, artificial intelligence, the Internet of Things, and the data center industry, the global market for advanced semiconductor packaging continues to expand, with demand for packaging substrates and various core process materials maintaining high-speed growth. The project involves a total investment of 2 billion yen. The production line is equipped with high-grade clean production equipment, and upon operation, dry film photoresist capacity will increase by 40%, supporting a doubling of production volume. Asahi Kasei has been conducting dry film slitting processing at the Tainan base since 1997; this expansion improves the localized delivery chain to meet the supply needs of Taiwan's semiconductor packaging industry cluster. The slitting process directly determines the precision of the finished film and delivery stability. Asahi Kasei's SUNFORT™ dry film is compatible with both traditional stepper exposure and laser direct imaging equipment, enabling ultra-high-precision circuit transfer on substrates and enhancing advanced packaging process performance. Asahi Kasei has positioned electronic materials as a core growth segment, continuously iterating packaging materials adapted for AI chips. In May 2025, it will launch the new generation SUNFORT™ TA dry film photoresist for advanced packaging adapted for AI servers; in May 2026, a new photosensitive polyimide film will be developed and launched. Customer validation is currently underway, and it will subsequently be used for packaging redistribution layers and substrate insulation layers, with commercialization expected. ... On July 2, Sumitomo Chemical officially announced that its wholly-owned Korean subsidiary, Dongwoo Fine-Chem, has signed a joint venture agreement with Samsung Electro-Mechanics to establish a new joint venture, Glassem, in 2026. Samsung Electro-Mechanics will hold 66% and Dongwoo Fine-Chem 34%. The JV will focus on the R&D, production, and sales of advanced packaging glass core substrates, integrating the material and substrate manufacturing technology reserves of both parties. The plan is to establish a complete supply system in the second half of fiscal 2027 and gradually expand production. ... Beyond the layout of glass substrates, Sumitomo Chemical's material capacities continue to land: in May 2026, a subsidiary will launch the world's first low α radiation spherical alumina, adapted for advanced packaging heat dissipation needs; in April, construction of the Osaka Advanced Photoresist Technology Center was launched, covering the R&D and production of EUV and ArF high-end photoresists, with expected completion by the end of 2027.

The company reported that while sales volumes in the Carbon segment were approximately 10 percent lower compared to the second quarter of last year, utilization in this segment remained at 69 percent. Management noted that expected improvements in utilization are anticipated toward the end of the year, following plans to restart a kiln in the U.S. The net impact of deferred shipments across various product groups was estimated at 10,000 to 15,000 metric tonnes. Looking ahead to the third quarter, volumes are expected to move back toward normal levels. The broader increase in primary aluminium production outside China is viewed as supportive for Rain's Carbon segment, and the company is actively engaging with customers to supply materials required for this growth. ... Regarding realized margins in the Carbon segment, management stated that while the quarter saw some opportunistic margins, these were not necessarily derived from traditional core products of the segment. The performance benefited from both product mix and market conditions rather than a single factor. The company noted a mixed product impact during the quarter: sales volumes were lower in carbon calcination but this was partially offset by higher carbon black oil sales in carbon distillation. In assessing the current market cycle, management emphasized that while the environment has improved from previous trough levels, it is not a return to pre-war conditions. The stability of CPC supply is supported by growing aluminium production outside China and constraints surrounding suitable anode-grade GPC availability. A key difference from prior price spikes was that the current cycle sees underlying support from structural demand growth and tighter raw material availability for smelters. ... The Advanced Materials segment, which includes Resins, Chemical Intermediates, and Engineered Products (including battery materials), saw performance supported by improved demand in several specialty end markets and disciplined cost-reduction measures implemented over recent years. Management views this segment as a platform for earning attractive returns through technology and formulation expertise rather than relying solely on commodity movements. On the topic of battery materials, Rain's strategy is focused on participating where its capabilities are relevant within the anode materials value chain. Activities include PETRORES specialty carbon coatings for battery anode production and the sale of mesophase carbon microbeads used in small-device batteries. Management maintains that significant progress depends on customer qualification timelines and disciplined capital allocation, viewing these areas as a long term opportunity. ... Concerning expansion, Rain has received permissions to undertake a new pitch production and distillation unit in India. The company plans to commence operations for the first phase of this distillation unit in early 2028, with the strategic rationale centering on enhancing supply reliability and local market serviceability within India's growing aluminium and carbon markets. When compared against integrated players, management emphasized that Rain’s competitive advantage lies in its sideways integration across CPC and CTP production, supported by global supply chain expertise and technical services. This positions the company not merely as a materials supplier but as a technical partner capable of assisting customers in managing quality and reliability in tighter market environments. ... Management acknowledged concerns regarding the Company's historical financial performance, noting that while the company has generated over ₹130,000 crore in revenue over the last decade and a half, cumulative profit was minimal, with operating cash flow significantly impacted by interest costs. Management stated that the current focus is on EBITDA normalization through improved utilization and operational efficiency. The company's immediate priorities are: - EBITDA normalization and operational efficiency improvement. - Balance sheet strengthening via deleveraging and working capital optimization. - Disciplined capital allocation, with a strong emphasis on cash returns and return on invested capital (ROIC). Regarding debt management, the company is in regular dialogue with banking advisors to assess refinancing opportunities. Management stated that they aim to manage toward a net-debt-to-EBITDA ratio of around 3x based on normalized earnings. Future excess cash generated will first be utilized to reduce working capital loans used for temporary safety stock builds before being applied to long term debt reduction. Concerning growth funding, management indicated there are no current plans to raise equity, preferring instead to improve cash generation, refinance strategically, and reduce leverage in a disciplined manner.

headline: RainFocus Launches Sales Module for Event-Driven Selling
summary_text: RainFocus Launches Sales Module for Event-Driven Selling # RainFocus Launches Sales Module for Event-Driven Selling RainFocus Jul 30, 2026, 09:30 ET The new module gives enterprise revenue leaders spend control, AE accountability, and cleaner data inputs for pipeline attribution LINDON, Utah, July 30, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- RainFocus™, provider of the next-generation event marketing platform, today announced the Sales Module, a purpose-built module that gives enterprise sales and events teams a governed, systemic way to run rep-driven event engagement. The module eliminates coordination challenges within event programs, including scattered attendee pass requests, limited quota visibility, and an inability to track whether sales reps are converting invitations into engagement. Organizations can now move beyond manual, siloed processes to create a unified strategy that drives pipeline and accelerates deals. RainFocus' new Sales Module gives enterprise revenue leaders spend control, AE accountability, and cleaner data inputs for pipeline attribution. How It Works The Sales Module integrates seamlessly with CRMs like Salesforce, creating a bi-directional data flow that enhances pre-event planning, engagement during the event, and post-event follow-up. Sales representatives can nominate contacts from their existing book of business, build personalized event agendas for any attendee (including prospects and VIP accounts), track real-time engagement activity, and invite contacts to exclusive ancillary events. Event activity data, including registration and session attendance, flows back into CRM campaigns, giving revenue teams a clean, standardized signal for the attribution model they already run and providing a reliable trigger for post-event outreach. ... - Governed Audience Acquisition: Systemizes contact nominations and approval processes, eliminating scattered pass requests. Business leaders can limit free and discounted passes, enforce quotas by region or business unit, and ensure controlled distribution. Events teams can then easily segment registration funds back to internal team funding. ... - Improved Attribution Inputs: By standardizing nomination, registration, and campaign-association data, Sales Module improves the quality of event data flowing into the CRM. It strengthens inputs available to the organization's current attribution model without replacing it. - Event Funding Engine: Sales Module enables direct tracking and attribution of event-generated revenue (e.g., ticket sales, internal department contributions) back to specific cost centers, creating a self-sustaining model for event investment. ... - "Events are no longer a cost center with soft outcomes; they are a measurable, governed sales channel that drives pipeline and accelerates deal cycles," said JR Sherman, CEO of RainFocus. "By bringing sales teams together with customer buying groups in a live environment, events provide the highest-fidelity touchpoints in the enterprise buying journey. RainFocus' Sales Module gives sales teams real-time access to engagement behavior and buying signals, empowering them to identify and execute the right next best action for every customer." - "For too long, events have been treated as a cost center rather than a growth engine," said Marius Milcher, VP of platform strategy and AI at RainFocus. "We're changing that narrative with the Sales Module. Governance, visibility, and accountability are now directly in the hands of sales and marketing leadership. This will fundamentally shift how enterprises think about event investment going forward." ... Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) What is the Sales Module? The Sales Module is a purpose-built module in the RainFocus platform that gives enterprise sales and events teams a governed, systematic way to run rep-driven event engagement. It integrates directly with CRMs like Salesforce, enabling AEs to nominate contacts, build personalized agendas for VIP accounts, and track engagement without leaving their existing workflow, while also giving leadership quota governance and activity visibility to ensure events are used strategically. What specific problem does the Sales Module solve for CROs? The Sales Module solves the governance and visibility gaps that make event investment difficult to control and justify. It gives sales leadership unified visibility into AE activity, tools to set and monitor pass quotas and spend by team or region, and data-driven insights to optimize how their teams engage at events. The result is events that are governed, measurable, and tied to a cleaner data foundation for any attribution model the organization already runs. How does the Sales Module contribute to the attribution of closed-won deals from event participation? The Sales Module provides a clean, governed data trail: registration, campaign association, nomination and approval history, sales-led activations at the event, executive meetings, networking activities, and more, tied to the right accounts and opportunities. That data strengthens organizations' existing attribution models and lets teams see which activations show up most often alongside closed-won deals. When a business unit or partner funds its own participation, that spend is tracked against the account and deal, supporting straightforward cost-recovery reporting. How does the Sales Module improve upon traditional CRM event integrations or manual processes? Unlike traditional integrations that typically sync contact lists after the fact, the Sales Module introduces governed workflow automation across the full event lifecycle, including nomination approvals, quota enforcement, in-event engagement tracking, and structured post-event data handoff. This eliminates manual coordination, reduces data silos, and gives sales reps the ability to customize event experiences for their most important customers. The group, whose public face is former Gazprom executive Igor Volobuev, identifies critical and vulnerable sections of Russian refineries and passes that information to the Ukrainian military. The Omsk facility was hit in a drone attack in early July 2026. The relevance for Indian companies lies in the white oil supply chain. headline: Cotiviti Retail Expands Contract Compliance Offering to Help Businesses Recover Lost Value, Protect Negotiated Terms and Savings | lifestyle.gooddecisions.com

headline: ​Exclusive: Rakuten and impact.com Form Strategic Alliance to Scale Connected Performance Ecosystem

headline: Management Buyout Completed at Impact Retail Group | LBV Hub

headline: ESSAR ENERGY TRANSITION RETAIL (“EET Retail”) ACQUIRES LEADING UK INDEPENDENT FORECOURT NETWORK SGN RETAIL - Essar
summary_text: # ESSAR ENERGY TRANSITION RETAIL (“EET Retail”) ACQUIRES LEADING UK INDEPENDENT FORECOURT NETWORK SGN RETAIL - Essar ... The SGN Retail acquisition creates a 235-site network with 650m+ litres of annual throughput — instantly making EET Retail the UK’s second-largest backward-integrated forecourt operator • Essar Energy Transition is building a leading integrated refinery-to-forecourt network, targeting 800 sites by 2031 — all supplied by Essar Energy Transition’s Stanlow refinery, which already produces [20]% of the UK’s road fuels • This reverses two decades of UK fuel market fragmentation, replacing an import-dependent, multi-layered supply chain with a direct refinery-to-pump model • UK-refined fuel will now reach UK forecourts directly — strengthening domestic energy security against global supply shocks and regional refinery closures • Essar Energy Transition is scaling the Essar brand’s forecourt offer — hot food, convenience, valeting and EV charging — as the platform grows toward national coverage STANLOW, CHESHIRE, 14 September 2026: EET Retail Limited (“EET Retail”), the retail division of Essar Energy Transition Fuels (“EET Fuels”), today announces an agreement to acquire 100% of SGN Retail, a leading UK independent forecourt operator founded by Graham Peacock and Susan Tobbell. The transaction adds 118 high-quality forecourt locations to EET Retail’s portfolio. Combined with EET Retail’s fast-growing existing estate of 117 sites, the transaction establishes a scaled, nationwide mobility platform of 235 fuel forecourts with annual throughput exceeding 650 million litres. ... Essar Energy Transition is committing to a model in the UK that integrates the manufacture of fuels with the sale of fuels to consumers in an efficient and reliable way. Over the last two decades, the UK market has fragmented between fuel retail and fuel production, as oil majors have significantly reduced their domestic refinery investments, leading to a complex and inefficient supply chain, often dependent on imports or complex domestic supply chains. EET Retail aims to challenge this dynamic in order to support an efficient and robust supply to UK customers. The transaction creates the second largest UK forecourt network that is backwardly integrated with fuel production. The acquisition of SGN Retail will substantially accelerate EET Retail’s long-term roadmap and strategic objective to scale its footprint to supply domestic fuel directly to 800 forecourts (~9% UK market share) by 2031. EET Retail believes that the combination of demographic growth, the rise of multi-car households and the declining number of forecourts in the UK create an attractive outlook to invest in the forecourt sector. ... Rerouting fuel refined at Stanlow directly into EET Retail forecourts boosts domestic supply security, by allowing UK refined fuel to be more efficiently distributed to domestic UK consumers. Furthermore, the integration of fuel production and sale will allow EET Retail to eliminate cost inefficiencies for motorists at the pump. ... The transaction will be funded through a combination of cash and a new £250m senior debt facility arranged by a bank group comprising First Abu Dhabi Bank, Macquarie Bank, Mizrahi Tefahot Bank, Natixis, OakNorth Bank, Royal Bank of Canada, SMBC Bank International and Sound Point Capital Management. ... Essar Energy Transition’s vision is to be a leading producer of low carbon fuels and establish a major energy transition hub in the North-West of England. Essar Energy Transition has an investment pipeline of £4.3 billion to develop a range of low carbon energy transition projects in the UK until 2035. Essar Energy Transition’s investment programme will play a key role in accelerating the UK’s low carbon transformation, supporting the government’s decarbonisation policy and creating highly skilled employment opportunities at the heart of the North-West. Essar Energy Transition Retail is the retail division of Essar Energy Transition Fuels (Essar Oil UK Ltd), established to build a nationwide network of premium, customer-focused service stations. Essar Energy Transition Fuels operates the Stanlow Manufacturing Complex in Cheshire, producing ~18% of UK transport fuels. ... Founded in 2016 by Graham Peacock and Susan Tobbell, SGN Retail manages 118 strategic roadside locations nationwide alongside leading retail, convenience, and food-to-go brands.

headline: Impact.com’s $340M Series D Is Rewriting the Partnership Platform Power Map – Affiliate Times
summary_text: Impact.com has closed a $340 million Series D round led by General Atlantic, signaling a high-stakes consolidation play in the partnership automation space that has rival networks scrambling. By Jake Sullivan · September 1, 2026 · 6 min read ... Impact.com confirmed Tuesday that it has closed a $340 million Series D funding round led by General Atlantic, with participation from existing investors Silversmith Capital Partners and a new strategic check from Publicis Groupe’s venture arm. The valuation was not disclosed publicly, but three sources with direct knowledge of the deal placed the figure north of $4.2 billion — a number that would make it one of the largest private valuations ever assigned to a performance-marketing infrastructure company. The announcement landed like a thunderclap at a moment when the affiliate and partnership industry is already processing compounding pressures: ITP-driven attribution erosion, the slow collapse of third-party cookie fallbacks, and a Federal Trade Commission that has been issuing civil investigative demands to performance networks at a pace not seen since the 2011 lead-gen crackdown. Against that backdrop, a $340 million war chest aimed squarely at enterprise advertiser acquisition is not a small signal — it is a reorientation of the entire competitive landscape. ... According to Impact.com CEO David A. Yovanno, the capital will be deployed across three strategic pillars: international market expansion — specifically Southeast Asia, LATAM, and the Gulf Cooperation Council region — deeper AI-native attribution tooling, and what the company is calling a “partnership intelligence” data layer that will sit above the tracking pixel and pull signals from first-party CRM integrations, SKAdNetwork data, and probabilistic fingerprinting where consent frameworks permit. ... Sources close to the deal say a meaningful portion of the Series D — potentially as much as $80 million — is earmarked for M&A. The targets being discussed internally, according to two people briefed on early board conversations, include mid-market affiliate networks in the APAC region and at least one fraud-detection SaaS company that has built proprietary device graph technology. ... For high-volume affiliates running on Impact’s platform, the funding news carries both upside and risk. The upside: better tooling, faster payments infrastructure, and potentially more competitive CPA payouts as Impact uses its balance sheet to recruit marquee advertisers who come with larger budgets and willingness to pay premium commissions. The risk is subtler but real. When platforms raise at unicorn-plus valuations, the pressure to demonstrate SaaS-style recurring revenue metrics typically accelerates a shift away from performance-only relationships toward retainer-based “managed partnership” tiers — which tend to favor large agency partners over independent super-affiliates who drive volume but resist monthly platform fees. Several top affiliates running finance and insurance verticals on Impact — where CPAs routinely run $90 to $340 per lead depending on product type — told Affiliate Times they are watching the fee structure closely. One media buyer generating over $2.1 million monthly in tracked revenue through Impact said anonymously: “The moment they restructure the publisher tier pricing to extract more margin from performance publishers, I am moving my top offers to direct relationships or to a network that still respects volume-based economics.” ... months into what privacy engineers are calling the “attribution dark age” — a period defined by Safari’s ITP decimating click-window tracking on iOS, Firefox’s ... party pixel matching, and Google’s own Privacy Sandbox APIs delivering conversion modeling accuracy that independent tests by Rockerbox and Northbeam have consistently rated at 60 to 74 percent fidelity compared to legacy pixel tracking. Impact’s bet — and the reason General Atlantic wrote the check — is that a platform with deep first-party integrations, server-side tracking infrastructure, and direct API connections to advertiser CRM systems can reconstruct attribution accuracy that cookie-dependent networks simply cannot match in a post-third-party-cookie world. - Server-side tracking adoption: Impact claims 34 percent of its top-1,000 advertiser accounts have migrated to full server-side event passing as of Q2 2026, up from 11 percent in Q2 2024. - Consent-mode coverage: The platform reports that 61 percent of EU-based advertiser accounts are now running Impact’s native consent-mode integration, a critical metric as GDPR enforcement actions against affiliate tracking have accelerated in Germany, France, and the Netherlands. - AI attribution modeling: The company’s “Intelligent Tracking” layer, launched in beta in March 2026, uses a gradient-boosted model trained on consented first-party signals to fill attribution gaps — currently deployed across 800 advertiser accounts in controlled rollout. ... Multiple sources indicate that compliance infrastructure is a significant internal priority attached to this raise. The FTC’s amended Endorsement Guides — effective January 2026 — have created substantial liability exposure for networks that cannot demonstrate they have actively audited their publisher bases for disclosure compliance. The Commission’s civil investigative demands, sent to at least four CPA networks this summer according to people with knowledge of the matter, specifically requested publisher communication logs and evidence of disclosure enforcement actions taken against non-compliant affiliates. ... Impact’s planned acquisition of fraud-detection technology is directly tied to this regulatory pressure. A platform that can demonstrate to the FTC — and to enterprise advertisers’ legal teams — that it is actively removing fraudulent publishers and enforcing disclosure policies has a structural sales advantage in the current climate that pure-performance networks without that paper trail do not. ... The more immediate consequence of this funding round for the broader industry is what it signals about consolidation velocity. When a platform at Impact’s scale raises at this level with explicit M&A intent, it forces every mid-tier network to make a binary decision: become an acquisition target on favorable terms now, or invest aggressively in differentiation before the window closes. Rakuten Advertising, which has been operating under persistent speculation about its parent company’s appetite for the affiliate unit, has reportedly had preliminary conversations with at least two private equity firms about a potential carve-out, according to one source familiar with those discussions. Rakuten Advertising declined to comment. ShareASale’s parent Awin, meanwhile, is understood to be accelerating its own product roadmap around publisher analytics — specifically a real-time EPC benchmarking dashboard that would give affiliates vertical-level performance comparisons across the Awin network — as a direct counter to Impact’s data-layer ambitions. For affiliate conference organizers and the broader ecosystem of tools companies — trackers, spy tools, landing-page builders — a better-capitalized Impact that is actively recruiting enterprise advertisers means larger budgets flowing into the tracked ecosystem, which historically lifts EPC averages across verticals as competition for quality publisher placements intensifies. Whether that rising tide lifts all boats or concentrates gains among Impact’s preferred publisher tier is the central question the industry will be watching through Q4 2026 and into next year’s budget cycle. The deal is expected to close formally by October 15, pending standard regulatory review. General Atlantic’s managing director will take a board observer seat as part of the terms.

headline: Impact Radius Rolls Out Dynamic Commission Engine for Enterprise Publishers – Affiliate Times
summary_text: Impact's new real-time commission adjustment system lets advertisers reward top-tier affiliates with automated payout bumps — and the early EPC data is turning heads across the network. By Rachel Morrison · August 27, 2026 · 7 min read ... Impact has quietly deployed what may be the most consequential infrastructure update in the enterprise affiliate network space since cross-device attribution went mainstream: a dynamic commission engine that allows advertisers to automatically adjust CPS payouts in real time based on publisher performance tiers, traffic quality scores, and conversion velocity. The rollout, confirmed by multiple Impact-connected sources and officially announced August 26, 2026, is already reshaping how performance-first brands structure their affiliate programs — and how top publishers negotiate their deals. The feature, internally codenamed “FlexCommission” during development and now branded as Impact’s Adaptive Payout Layer (APL), enables advertisers to define rule-based commission triggers that fire automatically when a publisher’s rolling 30-day EPC, approval rate, and new-customer ratio hit defined thresholds. The result: a publisher who was earning a flat 8% CPS commission can see that rate automatically step to 11% or 12% once their traffic clears quality benchmarks — without a single email to an affiliate manager. ... Once a publisher clears a ... , the payout adjustment fires ... Impact’s next reconciliation window — ... a four-hour cycle. Publishers see the updated ... reflected in their dashboard without needing to sign an amended ... , as A ... standing authorization model embedded in Impact’s updated publisher terms. ... Early access to APL was granted to a select group of Impact’s top advertisers in Q2 2026, including brands in the DTC health, home goods, and B2B SaaS verticals. The reaction from the publisher side has been sharply divided along a predictable fault line: large-volume affiliates are enthusiastic; mid-tier publishers running thinner margins are wary of the downside mechanics. The concern is legitimate. APL is bidirectional. Just as it automatically bumps payouts for over-performing publishers, it can step commissions down when performance falls below floor thresholds. An affiliate running aggressive paid traffic on a finance comparison offer, for instance, could see their 10% CPS rate drop to the program’s baseline 7% if their approval rate dips after a bad creative rotation — without any manual intervention from the advertiser’s affiliate team. ... Several STM Forum threads begun in ... past 48 hours have surfaced concern specifically around the approval-rate floor mechanic for affiliates running content-to-presell funnels on paid traffic. The consensus emerging from those ... : affiliates need to map every APL rule set before scaling spend on any APL-enabled ... , and sub-ID segmentation discipline is now non-negotiable for anyone who wants to protect their tier position ... Impact has confirmed that APL is currently activated for over 340 advertiser programs across its network as of the August 26 launch. The vertical breakdown skews heavily toward categories where new-customer attribution and LTV data are strong enough to support rule-based commissioning: - DTC subscription boxes and wellness brands — using new-customer percentage gates as the primary trigger - B2B SaaS via PartnerStack-competing programs — MRR milestone triggers, with commission bumps tied to activated trial conversion rates - Home improvement and home services lead-gen — approval rate plus geo-quality scoring - Travel and hospitality — booking-to-cancellation rate floors combined with GMV thresholds - Financial services (non-regulated comparison) — new-user rate and session quality scoring from Impact’s existing fraud-detection stack Notably absent from the early APL roster: iGaming, crypto exchanges, and sweepstakes — all verticals where Impact maintains stricter onboarding gates. Sources inside Impact suggest APL may be extended to iGaming programs operating in licensed jurisdictions in Q1 2027, pending regulatory review. ... The other negotiation dynamic worth watching: APL gives top publishers real-time visibility into exactly which metrics determine their payout rate. That transparency cuts both ways. Publishers can now optimize their traffic mix and sub-ID segmentation specifically to hit tier thresholds — which is exactly what Impact and advertisers want — but it also means publishers will push back hard on any APL rule set they view as artificially restrictive or structured to avoid paying out higher tiers. ... The honest answer is: it depends on how fast ... networks respond. CJ Affiliate has offered performance ... based commission tiers within its Flex Links and advertiser contract tooling for several cycles, but the automation layer has been manual and slow. Awin’s commission flexibility sits inside its Awin Access and MasterTag infrastructure, with dynamic rates theoretically achievable but rarely deployed at scale. Rakuten’s SmartHub technology handles some personalization at the creative and link level, but real-time commission automation is not a published capability. ... B2B SaaS ... , has offered ... typically require manual promotion by the partner ... manager rather than automated rule ... based triggering. Industry observers note that APL gives Impact a genuine differentiation lever when pitching enterprise advertisers who are currently split between Impact and CJ. For a DTC brand running a $2M annual affiliate program, the ability to automatically reward its top 20 publishers without staffing up its AM team is a material operational advantage. ... The broader picture is that Impact has made a deliberate bet that automation and data density can replace the relationship-driven commission negotiation that has defined affiliate network culture since the Commission Junction era. Whether that bet pays off will depend on how well advertisers design their APL rule sets — and how quickly the rest of the enterprise network stack responds. For now, APL is live, the early EPC lift data from beta programs is reportedly strong, and the affiliate industry has a new infrastructure variable to factor into every traffic and monetization decision.

headline: Michael Hill picks Impact Analytics for AI merchandise planning | The Datatech Times
summary_text: # Michael Hill picks Impact Analytics for AI merchandise planning The fine jewellery retailer will deploy Impact Analytics' AI-native platform across demand forecasting, replenishment and assortment planning in three markets. By The Datatech Times Editorial Team Mon, 3 August 2026 Michael Hill, the international fine jewellery retailer operating more than 280 stores across Australia, New Zealand and Canada, has selected Impact Analytics to overhaul its merchandise planning capabilities. The deployment will cover demand forecasting, inventory replenishment, store clustering and assortment planning, consolidating those functions onto a single AI-native SaaS platform. The contract follows a competitive evaluation process in which Michael Hill said it prioritised retail-specific AI maturity over general-purpose planning tools. Richard Price, Head of Supply Chain Systems at Michael Hill, cited confidence in the forecasting engine as a decisive factor, particularly for high-value, low-volume product categories such as fine jewellery. "Accurate forecasting underpins every planning decision we make, and the results we saw across our assortment reinforced that we had selected the right partner," he said. ... Matt Keays, Chief Technology Officer at Michael Hill, framed the change as a structural shift in how planning teams operate, moving from spreadsheet-driven, line-by-line analysis to an exceptions-management model. The company did not disclose contract value, implementation timeline or the name of any incumbent vendor being replaced. Impact Analytics, founded over a decade ago, positions its platform as purpose-built for retail rather than adapted from manufacturing or FMCG planning systems. The vendor says its platform is powered by more than one million machine learning models and covers end-to-end planning, pricing and promotions. The company has previously highlighted recognition from Inc. 5000 and the RIS Leaderboard, though independently verified benchmark comparisons were not included in the announcement. ... The retail merchandise planning software market is a well-established category with a number of significant vendors, including Blue Yonder, o9 Solutions, Relex Solutions and Anaplan, alongside newer AI-native challengers. Competition has intensified as legacy players have added machine learning layers to existing platforms, making it harder for buyers to distinguish genuine AI-native architecture from retrofitted capability. Jewellery retail presents specific forecasting challenges: relatively small unit volumes per SKU, high product value, long replenishment lead times and significant localisation requirements across geographically dispersed store networks. ... Because Impact Analytics processes transaction and inventory data across three jurisdictions, the deployment will need to satisfy data-handling requirements under Australia's Privacy Act, New Zealand's Privacy Act 2020 and Canada's PIPEDA, with the latter currently undergoing reform under Bill C-27. None of those obligations were addressed in the release, and Michael Hill's data-residency arrangements with the vendor are not publicly disclosed. The broader enterprise AI procurement context is also shifting: the EU AI Act's requirements for high-risk AI systems do not apply here, but both UK and Australian regulators have signalled interest in transparency obligations for algorithmic decision-making tools used in commercial settings. For now, retail planning AI sits outside mandatory disclosure regimes, but enterprise buyers are increasingly asking vendors for explainability documentation as part of their own governance frameworks.
